heading: agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions

You are **agent-vkai-master**, the orchestrating Claude Code session for the **VK AI Labs Insurance** ecosystem — a personal portfolio project spanning 4 independent repositories across two clouds (GCP client side, Azure provider side).

You do **not** write code yourself. Your job is to understand a new requirement (a "Story"), determine which specialized subagents are needed, sequence the work correctly, get explicit human approval before acting, delegate, and record the outcome.

---

heading: The ecosystem you're orchestrating
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## The ecosystem you're orchestrating
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## The ecosystem you're orchestrating

| Repo (folder) | Subagent | Cloud | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vkai-insurance-client/` | `subAgent-vkai-client` | GCP | Customer-facing React frontend |
| `vkai-insurance-client-api/` | `subAgent-vkai-client-api` | GCP | Client-side Node.js API + Postgres |
| `vkai-insurance-provider/` | `subAgent-vkai-provider` | Azure | Ops-facing React frontend |
| `vkai-insurance-provider-api/` | `subAgent-vkai-provider-api` | Azure | Provider-side Node.js API + Postgres |
| `vkai-insurance-automation/` | `agent-vkai-automation` | — (QA / live) | Selenium+Cucumber UI regression suite, run against the **live** client portal |
| Jira project `VJS` (no repo) | `agent-vkai-jira-update` | — | Test-case issues + execution reporting in Jira, via REST API |
| Jira project `VJS` (Story issues) | `agent-vkai-jira-story` | — | The parent **Story** issue only: fetch/parse scenarios, status transitions (To Do → In Progress → Done), dev/test summary comment + Test-Case links |

The two clouds are **fully independent** — no shared database, ever. They only communicate via HTTPS sync calls (a standard event envelope, shared-secret auth). Each repo has its own `BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` — **always read the relevant repo's own docs before deciding scope**, don't rely on this file's summary alone.

---

heading: The full subagent sequence (7 subagents)
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## The full subagent sequence (7 subagents)
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## The full subagent sequence (7 subagents)

The four app subagents above own product code and are chosen/ordered per story (usually API-before-frontend). Three more Jira/QA subagents **bracket** the story, and you invoke them **explicitly and in order — never autonomously, never as background triggers**:

- **`agent-vkai-jira-story`** — the **only** subagent permitted to write to the parent **Story** issue. Invoked **first**, in MODE 1 ("fetch"), to read/parse the Story's `## Scenario N:` / Given-When-Then blocks, transition it to **In Progress**, and return the scenarios as the story content (or, if the human later rejects the plan, to **roll the Story back to To Do**); and **last**, in MODE 2 ("close"), to post the dev/test/execution summary comment, link each new Test Case to the Story, and transition it to **Done**. It never touches a Test Case issue directly — that stays `agent-vkai-jira-update`'s job.

5. **`agent-vkai-automation`** — invoked **last, after the four app subagents succeed**. It decides whether the story introduces any new **client-side, UI-only** test case (provider-UI, API-level, manual, and DB scenarios are permanently out of scope), authors Gherkin + builds the automation with live-DOM-grounded locators, and — **only after you have the human confirm all four app repos are merged `dev` → `main`** — runs the suite live and produces the ExtentReport. If nothing UI-automatable applies, it says so and stops.
6. **`agent-vkai-jira-update`** — invoked **after** `agent-vkai-automation`, and **only if** it produced new cases/results. It takes that structured handoff and, via the Jira REST API, creates the VJS Test Case issue(s), transitions them to Done, and attaches the ExtentReport.

If `agent-vkai-automation` reports "nothing applies," there is no handoff — do **not** invoke `agent-vkai-jira-update`.

Then, as the **final step whenever new Jira issues were created**, re-invoke **`agent-vkai-automation` for a doc-reconciliation pass**: relay the exact scenario-ID → Jira-key mapping `agent-vkai-jira-update` returned, and have it replace the placeholder keys in the two `context/` regression docs with the real keys and refresh any now-stale scenario-count / scope language. This closes the loop that otherwise leaves those docs referencing placeholders forever.

The full per-story order is therefore: **agent-vkai-jira-story (MODE 1 "fetch") → [human approval gate] → [the needed app subagents, in dependency order] → agent-vkai-automation (build + live run) → agent-vkai-jira-update (create issues, report the real keys) → agent-vkai-automation (final doc-reconciliation pass with the real keys) → agent-vkai-jira-story (MODE 2 "close": summary comment, Test-Case links, → Done)**.

---

### Workflow for every new Story

heading: 0. Receive the Jira Story key
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 0. Receive the Jira Story key
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 0. Receive the Jira Story key

The human provides **only a Jira Story key** (e.g. `VJS-44`) — **no story text**. That key is the entire input; the scenario content lives inside the Story issue.

heading: 1. Fetch the Story — `agent-vkai-jira-story`, MODE 1 ("fetch")
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 1. Fetch the Story — `agent-vkai-jira-story`, MODE 1 ("fetch")
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 1. Fetch the Story — `agent-vkai-jira-story`, MODE 1 ("fetch")

Invoke **`agent-vkai-jira-story` in MODE 1 ("fetch")** with that key. It reads and parses the Story's `## Scenario N:` / Given-When-Then blocks, transitions the Story to **In Progress**, and returns the summary + parsed scenarios + Story key. If it reports the description is **malformed**, stop and surface that to the human — never fabricate story content.

heading: 2. Assign numbers and record both
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 2. Assign numbers and record both
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 2. Assign numbers and record both

Take the returned scenarios as the story content. Open `Story.md` at this folder's root, find the highest existing `VKAI-XXX` and assign the next one (start at `VKAI-001` if empty). **Record the Jira Story key (e.g. `VJS-44`) alongside it — `Story.md` now carries both numbers.**

heading: 3. Understand, scope, and order
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 3. Understand, scope, and order
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 3. Understand, scope, and order

Read the relevant repos' `BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md` files to ground the work in what exists today. Decide which of the 4 app subagents are genuinely needed and in what **dependency order** (the contract-defining side — usually an API — before its consumer; genuinely independent subagents may run in parallel). A story might touch just one repo, one full-stack side, or — only when truly required — all four. **If anything is ambiguous** — unclear requirement, missing detail, a design decision only the human can make — **stop and ask**. Never guess on ambiguous scope.

heading: 4. Present the plan and get approval — HARD STOP
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 4. Present the plan and get approval — HARD STOP
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 4. Present the plan and get approval — HARD STOP

Present to the human: the assigned **VKAI-XXX and the Jira Story key**, which subagents will run in what order (or noted as parallel), what each will be asked to do, and any assumptions you're making. **Do not invoke any app subagent until the human explicitly approves.**
- **If REJECTED:** invoke **`agent-vkai-jira-story`'s ROLLBACK path** (revert the Story to **To Do**, log why via a short comment), then **stop**. Do not proceed further.
- **If APPROVED:** continue.

heading: 5. Invoke the app subagent(s)
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 5. Invoke the app subagent(s)
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 5. Invoke the app subagent(s)

For each needed app subagent, pass complete context in the prompt — subagents start with a fresh context window and only see what you give them: the VKAI-XXX / Story key, the specific task, and any output from a prior subagent it depends on (e.g. new field names an API subagent added that its frontend now consumes). After each completes, review its summary and confirm success (real commit pushed to `dev`, no errors) before the next. **Keep a short record of what each app subagent reported** — you assemble the MODE 2 dev summary from it in step 7.

heading: 6. Invoke the QA tail
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 6. Invoke the QA tail
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 6. Invoke the QA tail

In order: **`agent-vkai-automation`** (build + live run — the live run **only after the human confirms all four app repos are merged `dev` → `main`**) → **`agent-vkai-jira-update`** (create Test Case issues, report the real scenario-ID → Jira-key mapping) → **`agent-vkai-automation`** (final doc-reconciliation pass with the real keys). If automation reports **"nothing applies,"** there is no handoff — skip `agent-vkai-jira-update` and the reconciliation pass.

heading: 7. Close the Story — `agent-vkai-jira-story`, MODE 2 ("close")
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 7. Close the Story — `agent-vkai-jira-story`, MODE 2 ("close")
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 7. Close the Story — `agent-vkai-jira-story`, MODE 2 ("close")

Invoke **`agent-vkai-jira-story` in MODE 2 ("close")**, passing:
- a short **high-level dev summary** assembled from what the app subagents reported in step 5 (what changed, repos touched — **not** implementation detail),
- the **count of new test cases** from `agent-vkai-automation`, and
- the **pass/fail totals + Jira Test Case keys** from `agent-vkai-jira-update`.

It posts one summary comment (Development Completed → Test Design Completed → Test Execution Completed → Test Cases:), links each Test Case to the Story, and transitions the Story to **Done**. (If the QA tail produced no new cases, still close the Story — pass a zero test-case count and no keys; the comment records zero cases and there are simply no Test-Case links.)

heading: 8. Record the outcome
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 8. Record the outcome
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 8. Record the outcome

Append a new entry to `Story.md` (see that file's format section) summarizing: the story, subagents involved, commits made, new VJS Test Case issues, the live-run result + ExtentReport, and what — if anything — still needs human action (typically: merging each affected repo's `dev` → `main` PR) — **now including the Jira Story key from step 2**. Do this **after** the QA tail **and** the MODE 2 close have reported back. **If new Jira issues were created, ensure the final `agent-vkai-automation` doc-reconciliation pass ran (real keys swapped for placeholders, counts refreshed) *before* logging**, and note in the entry that the two `context/` docs were reconciled.

heading: 9. Tell the human what's left
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 9. Tell the human what's left
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Workflow for every new Story > ### 9. Tell the human what's left

Remind them explicitly that you never merge PRs — that's always a manual step they need to do per affected repo. Also, **whenever the two `context/` regression docs (`vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md`, `vkai-insurance-regression-automation-v1.md`) changed during the story, end your summary with an explicit reminder to re-upload both to the Claude.ai Project** — they live only in the local `context/` folder, are not git-tracked, and are otherwise invisible to the Project.

---

heading: Hard rules — never violate these
breadcrumb: # agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Hard rules — never violate these
text:
# agent-vkai-master — Orchestration Instructions > ## Hard rules — never violate these

1. **Never invoke a subagent without explicit human approval of the plan first — except `agent-vkai-jira-story` MODE 1 ("fetch"), which necessarily runs before the plan exists, since its output is what the plan is built from.**
2. **Never let a subagent open or merge a pull request.** Subagents commit and push to their own `dev` branch only. PR review and merging is always the human's job.
3. **Never guess on ambiguous requirements.** Ask.
4. **Never write or edit code yourself.** That's what subagents are for.
5. **Never let a subagent touch a repo other than its own.** If a story seems to require one subagent to modify a sibling repo's files, that's a sign you need to invoke that sibling's own subagent instead.
6. **Always log the story to `Story.md`, even if it was small or only touched one repo.**
7. **The QA-tail subagents are invoked explicitly by you, in order, never autonomously:** the needed app subagents → `agent-vkai-automation` → `agent-vkai-jira-update`. Never invoke `agent-vkai-jira-update` when automation reported "nothing applies."
8. **Never let `agent-vkai-automation` run the live suite until the human confirms all four app repos are merged `dev` → `main`.** Keep its scope to the automation repo + the two `context/` regression docs — never the app repos, never Jira, never `Story.md`.
9. **`agent-vkai-jira-update` touches only Jira (project `VJS`) via REST — never any repo's code and never `Story.md`.** Its credentials come from the environment / gitignored local config; never request or accept the API token in chat.
10. **When a story creates new Jira issues, the last step is always the `agent-vkai-automation` doc-reconciliation pass** — relay the real scenario-ID → Jira-key mapping so placeholders in the two `context/` regression docs become real keys and stale scenario-count/scope language is refreshed. Never end a story with placeholder keys left in those docs. And whenever those two local-only docs changed, **end the user-facing summary with a reminder to re-upload both to the Claude Project.**
11. **`agent-vkai-jira-story` is the only subagent permitted to write to the parent Story issue.** No other subagent — **including `agent-vkai-jira-update`** — ever transitions or comments on a Story issue. `agent-vkai-jira-update` stays on **Test Case** issues; `agent-vkai-jira-story` stays on the **Story** issue.

heading: VKAI-001: Add non-editable "Key" field to policy catalog plans
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Story Log > ## VKAI-001: Add non-editable "Key" field to policy catalog plans
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Story Log > ## VKAI-001: Add non-editable "Key" field to policy catalog plans

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Raw request:** A new field 'key' to be introduced while creating a new plan under policy catalog and is to be entertained everywhere. Given the Provider Portal Add Plan screen under Policy Catalog: when the user enters 'Name' and clicks Save Plan, then a new non-editable "Key" field is presented below 'Name', auto-populated with the first letters of each word and any digit, remaining locked; and 'Key' is added as a prefix to 'Name' in the catalog list. (Submitted labelled "VKAI-101"; assigned VKAI-001 as the first entry in the log.)

**Subagents involved (in order):** subAgent-vkai-provider-api → subAgent-vkai-provider
**Clarifying questions asked:**
- *Key generation algorithm?* → First character of each whitespace-separated token of the Name, uppercased (e.g. "Premium Gold 2024" → "PG2").
- *How far does "everywhere" reach?* → Provider side only; client API and customer-facing app left unchanged.
- *Unique keys or allow duplicates?* → Enforce uniqueness (server-side, numeric suffix on collision).
- *Backfill existing plans or new only?* → Backfill all existing plans.
- *Story number?* → Log was empty, assigned VKAI-001.

**Outcome:**
| Subagent | Repo | Branch | Commit(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| subAgent-vkai-provider-api | vkai-insurance-provider-api | dev | `9b6f443` | ✅ Done |
| subAgent-vkai-provider | vkai-insurance-provider | dev | `fcd62c0` | ✅ Done |

**Summary:**
- **vkai-insurance-provider-api:** Added a unique `key` column to `policy_catalog` (Prisma migration that adds nullable → backfills → sets NOT NULL + unique index). New `src/lib/policyKey.js` derives the key (first char of each name token, uppercased) and enforces uniqueness with a dash-numeric suffix scheme (`PG2`, `PG2-2`, `PG2-3`…). `POST /v1/policy-catalog` derives/persists/returns `key`; `GET /v1/policy-catalog` includes `key` per row. The cross-cloud `GET /v1/catalog/policies` endpoint was given an explicit `select` to *exclude* `key`, keeping the client cache byte-for-byte unchanged (honoring "provider side only"). No sync/envelope logic touched. Backfill runs at deploy time (no live DB reachable in the build env, so no row count captured).
- **vkai-insurance-provider:** On the Add Plan screen, after Save the form reveals a read-only, locked "Key" field below Name populated from the API response (pre-save placeholder: "Generated automatically after you save"), then swaps Save for a "Done" button. The catalog list renders `key` as a styled prefix to the plan name (`PG2 - Premium Gold 2024`). Edit form also shows the existing key read-only. Approver-only gating unchanged. Production build passes.

**Follow-ups needed:**
- Merge `dev` → `main` on **vkai-insurance-provider-api** (manual PR).
- Merge `dev` → `main` on **vkai-insurance-provider** (manual PR).
- On first deploy, confirm the backfill migration ran and the create-response `key` renders in a real browser session (couldn't be verified end-to-end without a live DB + Entra ID login).

**Documentation catch-up (2026-08-03):** After the code shipped, both provider repos' own docs were updated to reflect the `key` field (docs-only, no code changes).
| Subagent | Repo | Branch | Commit | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| subAgent-vkai-provider-api | vkai-insurance-provider-api | dev | `43ac755` | BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md (business rule) + CLAUDE.md (algorithm, `src/lib/policyKey.js` helpers, deliberate exclusion of `key` from cross-cloud `GET /v1/catalog/policies`, intentional presence on ops `GET /v1/policies`) |
| subAgent-vkai-provider | vkai-insurance-provider | dev | `767c873` | BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md (business rule) + CLAUDE.md (key is server-side/read-only, Add-Plan reveal-after-save flow, list prefix rendering) |

These doc commits are additional to the merges already listed above — the same two `dev` → `main` merges now also carry the documentation updates.

heading: VKAI-002: Extend the `key` feature end-to-end to the client portal
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Story Log > ## VKAI-002: Extend the `key` feature end-to-end to the client portal
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Story Log > ## VKAI-002: Extend the `key` feature end-to-end to the client portal

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Raw request:** Extend the "key" feature from VKAI-001 across the full E2E system, including the client portal. This intentionally reverses the VKAI-001 scope decision that excluded `key` from the cross-cloud catalog endpoint so it wouldn't reach the client. `key` must flow to the client for both the cached policy catalog and any enrolled policy, for existing and new records. On the client Catalog page and Dashboard/"Your policies" list, every plan/policy shows its `key` as a name prefix; nested premium/claim line items are not prefixed; the client never generates `key` (read-through only); no changes to enrollment/premium/claim sync payloads (`key` is catalog-display-only, not a field on `policies`/`premiums`/`claims`).

**Subagents involved (in order):** subAgent-vkai-provider-api → subAgent-vkai-client-api → subAgent-vkai-client
**Clarifying questions asked:** None — the story was prescriptive on all business decisions. Plan presented and human-approved before invoking.

**Outcome:**
| Subagent | Repo | Branch | Commit(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| subAgent-vkai-provider-api | vkai-insurance-provider-api | dev | `5a3af18` | ✅ Done |
| subAgent-vkai-client-api | vkai-insurance-client-api | dev | `401071a` | ✅ Done |
| subAgent-vkai-client | vkai-insurance-client | dev | `4936e49` | ✅ Done |

**Summary:**
- **vkai-insurance-provider-api:** Reversed the VKAI-001 exclusion — added `key: true` to the explicit `select` on the cross-cloud `GET /v1/catalog/policies` so each catalog row now returns `key` (string, non-null). Envelope/auth/other sync logic unchanged. Docs updated to mark the VKAI-001 exclusion gotcha as superseded.
- **vkai-insurance-client-api:** Added a nullable `key` column to the **cached catalog** table only (migration); catalog refresh (`refreshCatalogFromProvider`, upsert on `providerPolicyId`) now persists `key`, updating pre-existing cached rows in place. `GET /v1/catalog` exposes `key` per row; `GET /v1/policies` exposes a top-level `key` per policy resolved from the catalog relation (no `key` column added to `policies`; nested premiums/claims unaffected; degrades to null if unresolved). Added a force-refresh capability `npm run catalog:refresh` (`scripts/refresh-catalog.js`) that bypasses the 15-min staleness gate. No sync payloads changed. Docs updated.
- **vkai-insurance-client:** Added a shared `formatPlanName(key, name)` helper; the Catalog page and the Dashboard "Your policies" card headings render `key` as a `KEY - Name` prefix. Nested premium/claim line items are not prefixed. Null/blank key falls back to the bare name with no separator; the client never generates a key. Docs updated.

**Follow-ups needed:**
- Merge `dev` → `main` on all three repos: **vkai-insurance-provider-api**, **vkai-insurance-client-api**, **vkai-insurance-client** (manual PRs).
- At deploy: the client-api migration applies via `prisma migrate deploy`; then run the force-refresh where the provider API is reachable so pre-existing cached catalog rows pick up their `key` immediately — `docker compose exec api npm run catalog:refresh` (otherwise they backfill on the next natural staleness refresh).
- Verify end-to-end in a real browser (live DB + provider reachable) — not possible from the build sandbox.
- **Out-of-scope note / optional follow-up:** the client single-policy **detail page** (`src/pages/PolicyDetail.jsx`) heading was deliberately NOT prefixed, since the story scoped display to the Catalog page and the "Your policies" list. Decide separately if you want the prefix there too. → **Resolved, see follow-up below.**

**Follow-up (2026-08-03) — PolicyDetail prefix:** Per human request, the key prefix was added to the client's individual PolicyDetail page heading too, for consistency. Single repo, no backend changes (client API already exposes `key`).
| Subagent | Repo | Branch | Commit | Change |

| subAgent-vkai-client | vkai-insurance-client | dev | `91523cd` | `PolicyDetail.jsx` heading now uses the shared `formatPlanName(policy.key ?? catalog.key, name)` helper to show the `KEY - Name` prefix; nested premium/claim items unprefixed; docs updated. |

This follow-up rides along on the same `vkai-insurance-client` `dev` → `main` merge already listed above.

heading: VKAI-003: Push-based catalog sync (provider → client), pull kept as fallback
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Story Log > ## VKAI-003: Push-based catalog sync (provider → client), pull kept as fallback
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Story Log > ## VKAI-003: Push-based catalog sync (provider → client), pull kept as fallback

**Date:** 2026-08-13
**Raw request:** Change policy catalog sync from pull-based (client refreshes on stale cache/page load) to push-based, so a new/edited catalog entry on the provider reflects on the client immediately with no wait. Add an outbound sync call from vkai-insurance-provider-api on catalog create/edit, following the same shared-secret + event-envelope + idempotency pattern as the existing enrollment/premium/claim sync flows. Add the corresponding inbound endpoint on vkai-insurance-client-api. Keep the existing stale-cache pull as a fallback, don't remove it. No changes to client UI or provider UI unless found otherwise. Sequence: provider-api → client-api.

**Subagents involved (in order):** subAgent-vkai-provider-api → subAgent-vkai-client-api
**Clarifying questions asked:** None — story was prescriptive; plan presented and human-approved before invoking.

**Outcome:**
| Subagent | Repo | Branch | Commit(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| subAgent-vkai-provider-api | vkai-insurance-provider-api | dev | `cc6ca05` | ✅ Done |
| subAgent-vkai-client-api | vkai-insurance-client-api | dev | `99a637a` | ✅ Done |

**Contract established:** `POST /v1/sync/catalog` on the client API, guarded by the `X-VKAI-Sync-Key` shared secret. Snake_case envelope (`event_id`, `event_type: "catalog.upserted"`, `occurred_at`, `source: "provider"`, `payload`); **camelCase** payload (`id`, `key`, `name`, `description`, `premiumAmount`/`coverageAmount` as decimal strings, `isActive`, `createdAt`) — deliberately mirroring the pull response. Dedupe/upsert on `payload.id` → client's `providerPolicyId`. A single `catalog.upserted` event covers create, edit, and deactivate.

**Summary:**
- **vkai-insurance-provider-api:** `POST /v1/policy-catalog` (create) and `PATCH /v1/policy-catalog/:id` (edit/deactivate) now fire an outbound push (`catalog.upserted`) to the client's `/v1/sync/catalog`, reusing the existing outbound-sync mechanism. Extended the per-row reliability trio (`sync_status`/`sync_attempts`/`event_id`) to the `policy_catalog` table via a migration that backfills pre-existing rows to `synced` (so the retry sweep doesn't re-push the whole catalog on first deploy). The 5-min cron `retrySync` now also retries catalog rows. Local ops action always succeeds even if the push fails. Pull endpoint `GET /v1/catalog/policies` unchanged (fallback). Docs updated.
- **vkai-insurance-client-api:** Added inbound `POST /v1/sync/catalog` guarded by the same `syncAuth` shared-secret middleware. Extracted the pull's mapping into a shared `upsertCatalogItem()` now used by both the push route and the periodic pull refresh (one upsert path, idempotent on `providerPolicyId`). No separate `event_id` log — matches the repo's existing idempotent-state pattern. Stale-cache pull fallback fully intact; VKAI-002 `key` support works through both paths. Docs updated.

**Behavior change to note:** to make deactivation take effect, the client-api added `where: { isActive: true }` to its customer-facing `GET /v1/catalog` queries. Previously that route returned all cached rows unfiltered, but since the pull only ever stored active rows this was effectively a no-op before — now a pushed `isActive: false` immediately removes a plan from the customer browse catalog. Existing customer policies referencing a deactivated plan are unaffected (only the browse list is filtered).

**Follow-ups needed:**
- Merge `dev` → `main` on both **vkai-insurance-provider-api** and **vkai-insurance-client-api** (manual PRs).
- At deploy: the provider-api migration (`20260813000000_add_policy_catalog_sync`) applies via `prisma migrate deploy` and backfills existing catalog rows to `sync_status = 'synced'`. No new env vars — both sides reuse the existing shared-secret config.
- Verify end-to-end with both clouds reachable (create/edit/deactivate a plan on the provider and confirm the client reflects it immediately without waiting for the staleness window) — not possible from the build sandbox.

Let the automation suite set up **policy preconditions** the client UI can't produce on its own
— an `active` or `expired` policy, and a specific `expiry_date` — **without** invoking the
Entra-gated Approver actions. This unlocks the 9 active/expired-policy-blocked client scenarios.

`activate` / `approve` / `reject` / `mark-paid` and all claims transitions **remain manual** and

# Provider-API Test-Fixture Endpoints — Spec > ## Hard gating (both required)

1. **Env flag** — mount the fixture router only when
   `VKAI_INSURANCE_PROVIDER_API_ENABLE_TEST_FIXTURES=true`. Absent/false ⇒ routes 404 (as if not
   present). **Never set in prod** (verify prod `docker-compose.yml` / CI env never sets it).
2. **Fixture secret** — require header `X-VKAI-Test-Fixture-Key`, compared to
   `VKAI_INSURANCE_PROVIDER_API_TEST_FIXTURE_KEY`. Distinct from the sync key and from Entra.
   Missing/wrong ⇒ 401.

Per repo convention, add both new env vars to **`.env.example` AND** the `api` service's
`environment:` block in `docker-compose.yml` (but leave them unset/false in prod).

### Endpoint

heading: `POST /v1/test-fixtures/policies/state`
breadcrumb: # Provider-API Test-Fixture Endpoints — Spec > ## Endpoint > ### `POST /v1/test-fixtures/policies/state`
text:
# Provider-API Test-Fixture Endpoints — Spec > ## Endpoint > ### `POST /v1/test-fixtures/policies/state`

Set a mirrored policy's status and/or expiry, and **propagate to the client** so the client UI
reflects it.

Request:
```json
{
  "client_policy_id": "5ea11f4b-bc2d-4fdb-84fe-1fd6639a486d",
  "status": "active",          // one of: pending | active | expired  (optional)
  "expiry_date": "2027-08-13"  // ISO date (optional); at least one of status/expiry_date required
}
```
- The suite obtains `client_policy_id` from the client dashboard card link
  (`<a href="/policies/<client_policy_id>">`), so lookup is by `clientPolicyId` (already stored on
  the provider's mirrored policy from `POST /v1/sync/policies`).

Behavior:
1. Find the provider `policies` row by `clientPolicyId` → 404 if none.
2. Update `status` and/or `expiryDate` on that row.
3. **Propagate to the client** (this is the important part — the client UI reads the *client* DB):
   - status → reuse the existing client callback the activate flow already uses:
     `POST /v1/sync/policies/status` (via `services/clientSync.js`).
   - expiry_date → push via the existing renewal path (`POST /v1/sync/policies`,
     `event_type: policy.renewed`), which the client already handles for renewals.
4. Respond `200` with the updated provider policy (and sync outcome).

Constraints:
- Idempotent — repeating the same call is safe.
- **Policy state only.** No claim transitions, no premium/claim creation (those come through the
  normal client UI). `status` limited to `pending|active|expired`.
- No `ops_user` attribution — it is not an ops action.

  (review/approve/reject/mark-paid). Those stay manual.

- The client UI reads the **client** DB, so propagation (step 3) is essential. Confirm the client's
  inbound handlers persist what we push — in particular that an `expiry_date` update lands
  client-side (the `policy.renewed` path should, but verify; a small `vkai-insurance-client-api`
  check may be needed).
- Automation side (separate, in this repo, once endpoints exist): add
  `VKAI_PROVIDER_FIXTURE_BASE_URL` + `VKAI_PROVIDER_FIXTURE_KEY` to `ConfigReader`, and a small
  HTTP client to call the fixture between UI steps. No Selenium involved for the fixture call.

heading: What this repo is
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## What this repo is
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## What this repo is

`vkai-insurance-client` is the **customer-facing web frontend** of *VK AI Labs Insurance* —
a personal portfolio project that demonstrates a realistic, **dual-cloud insurance platform**.
It is the app a customer actually uses: they sign up, browse a catalog of insurance policies,
enroll in the ones they want, pay their premiums, and file and track claims.

This is a demonstration project, not a commercial product. Its purpose is to show how a
complete insurance workflow can be built across two independent cloud providers that
cooperate without ever trusting each other's databases.

heading: Why it exists — the dual-cloud story
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Why it exists — the dual-cloud story
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Why it exists — the dual-cloud story

The platform is deliberately split into two fully independent halves that run on **different
clouds**:

- **Client side (GCP)** — this repo (`vkai-insurance-client`) and its backend
  (`vkai-insurance-client-api`). This is the customer's world: accounts, enrollments,
  premium payments, and claims.
- **Provider side (Azure)** — a separate app and API (`vkai-insurance-provider` /
  `vkai-insurance-provider-api`). This is the insurer's world: it defines the products on
  offer and adjudicates claims.

The two sides **never share a database**. There is no common datastore, no cross-cloud SQL,
no shared schema. They communicate **only over HTTPS API calls**, syncing state back and
forth. The client side owns its own copy of the data that matters to customers; the provider
side owns its own copy of the data that matters to the insurer. When something changes on one
side that the other needs to know about, it is pushed over the wire and reconciled — not read
directly out of a shared table.

This separation is the whole point of the demo: it mirrors how two organizations (or two
business units) with separate infrastructure and separate trust boundaries can still deliver
one coherent product to the end user.

heading: A key architectural decision: the catalog is provider-defined
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Why it exists — the dual-cloud story > ### A key architectural decision: the catalog is provider-defined
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Why it exists — the dual-cloud story > ### A key architectural decision: the catalog is provider-defined

The **policy catalog is owned by the provider (Azure) side**, not created by the client.
Customers can only enroll in policies the provider has published. The client side keeps a
**cached, read-only-from-its-POV copy** of that catalog (refreshed from the provider through
the client API), and enrollment always references a provider-defined catalog entry rather
than inventing a policy on the fly.

Practically, this means:

- Customers **choose from** a catalog; they never **define** a policy.
- Premium and coverage amounts, policy names, and descriptions originate on the provider side.
- The client experience is "shop the shelf and enroll," not "design your own insurance."

heading: Plan `key` prefix (display-only, provider-owned)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Why it exists — the dual-cloud story > ### A key architectural decision: the catalog is provider-defined > #### Plan `key` prefix (display-only, provider-owned)
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Why it exists — the dual-cloud story > ### A key architectural decision: the catalog is provider-defined > #### Plan `key` prefix (display-only, provider-owned)

Each catalog entry carries a provider-defined `key` (e.g. `PG2`, or a collision-suffixed
`PG2-2`). It originates on the provider side, syncs to the client side, and the client API
exposes it. The **client never generates or fabricates a key** — it only displays what the
API returns (a read-through of provider data).

Where it shows:

- **Catalog page** — each plan renders its `key` as a prefix on the plan name, e.g.
  `PG2 - Premium Gold 2024`. Read from the `key` field on each catalog row.
- **Dashboard / "Your policies"** — each enrolled policy renders its plan's `key` as a prefix
  on the **policy card heading only**. Read from the **top-level `key`** on each policy object
  (already resolved from the catalog by the API). Nested premium and claim line items under a
  policy card are **not** individually prefixed.
- **Policy detail page** (`/policies/:id`) — the single policy's plan name renders its `key`
  as a prefix on the **main page heading only**. Read from the **top-level `key`** on the
  policy object, falling back to the nested `policyCatalog.key`. Nested premium and claim line
  items on this page are **not** individually prefixed.

When `key` is `null`/absent/blank (e.g. a catalog entry not yet refreshed), the name is shown
with **no prefix and no stray separator**.

heading: Where this repo sits (and what it deliberately doesn't know)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Where this repo sits (and what it deliberately doesn't know)
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Where this repo sits (and what it deliberately doesn't know)

This repo talks to exactly **one thing**: its own backend, `vkai-insurance-client-api`. It has
**no knowledge of the provider side at all** — no provider URLs, no provider credentials, no
assumptions about Azure. Anything that ultimately needs the provider (publishing the catalog,
moving a claim through review, confirming a status) is the client API's job: *this frontend
calls the client API, and the client API talks to the provider API.*

Keeping the frontend ignorant of the provider is intentional. It keeps the trust boundary
clean and means the customer-facing app only ever depends on a single, stable contract.

heading: Core user journeys
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Core user journeys
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Core user journeys

1. **Sign up / log in** — A customer creates an account or signs in with email and password
   (Firebase Authentication). Their identity token is attached to every request to the client
   API, which creates the local customer record on first authenticated use.

2. **Browse the catalog** — The customer views the available policies (name, description,
   premium amount, coverage amount) — the provider-defined products described above.

3. **Enroll in a policy** — The customer enrolls in a catalog policy. A new policy is created
   on the client side (starting as `pending`) and synced outbound to the provider.

4. **Pay a premium** — For an active policy, the customer records a premium payment. This is
   **virtual/simulated** — there is no real payment gateway and no real money moves; it
   mirrors exactly what the API models, which is enough to demonstrate the workflow.

5. **File a claim** — For an active policy, the customer files a claim with an amount and a
   description. The claim is created on the client side and synced to the provider for
   adjudication.

6. **Track a claim's status** — A claim moves through a lifecycle the customer can watch:

   ```
   Submitted → Under Review → Approved / Rejected → Paid
   ```

   The provider drives these transitions (that's its job — adjudication), and the resulting
   status is synced back to the client side and shown to the customer, color-coded for clarity.

7. **Renew near expiry** — When a policy is close to its expiry date (within 30 days), the
   customer is offered a **Renew** action that extends the term.

heading: Dashboard policy summary
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Dashboard policy summary
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Dashboard policy summary

Above the "Your policies" list, the dashboard shows two always-visible summary
boxes: a count of the customer's **Active** policies and a count of their
**Pending** policies. These counts are **derived entirely client-side** from the
policy data the dashboard already loads (`GET /v1/policies`) — there is no extra
API call and no new endpoint. Counting matches on the policy `status` value
compared case-insensitively (status arrives lowercase, e.g. `active`/`pending`,
even though the status pill displays it capitalized). Both boxes always render:
when a status has no policies, its box shows `0` rather than being hidden.

heading: Dashboard policy sections (Active vs Pending)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Dashboard policy sections (Active vs Pending)
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Dashboard policy sections (Active vs Pending)

Below the summary boxes, the customer's enrolled policies are shown in **two
separate sections**, each under its own always-visible heading:

1. **"Your Active Policies"** (first section)
2. **"Your Pending Policies"** (second section)

The split is **derived entirely client-side** from the already-loaded policy data
(`GET /v1/policies`) — no extra API call, no new endpoint — using the same
case-insensitive `status` matching as the summary counts (status arrives
lowercase):

- **"Your Pending Policies"** = policies whose `status` (lowercased) is `pending`.
- **"Your Active Policies"** = **all other (non-pending) policies** — `active`
  plus any other status (e.g. expired/cancelled/renewed). Nothing is ever hidden;
  every policy appears in **exactly one** of the two sections.

Both section headings **always render**, even when a bucket is empty. An empty
bucket shows a short message ("No active policies." / "No pending policies.")
instead of a policy grid. This two-section layout only applies when the customer
has at least one policy; when they have **no policies at all**, the existing
whole-page empty state ("No policies yet / Browse the catalog") takes precedence
and is shown instead of the two sections.

heading: Scope boundaries
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Scope boundaries
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Client Portal) > ## Scope boundaries

- **No real payments.** Premium payment is simulated end-to-end.
- **No policy authoring on the client.** Customers enroll in provider-defined catalog
  policies only.
- **No provider knowledge here.** This repo never contacts or reasons about the Azure side
  directly — only its own client API does.
- **Demonstration project.** The goal is to showcase the dual-cloud, no-shared-database
  architecture and the full customer journey, not to be a production insurance system.

heading: ⚠️ Critical gotcha: API responses are camelCase
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## ⚠️ Critical gotcha: API responses are camelCase
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## ⚠️ Critical gotcha: API responses are camelCase

The `vkai-insurance-client-api` backend uses **Prisma**, and its JSON responses come back in
**camelCase** — even though the underlying Postgres columns are snake_case. When reading API
data, **never assume snake_case**. Use:

- `premiumAmount`, `coverageAmount`, `isActive`, `lastSyncedAt` (catalog)
- `enrolledAt`, `expiryDate`, `policyCatalog` (nested), `premiums`, `claims` (policies)
- `amountClaimed`, `submittedAt`, `paidAt` (claims / premiums)

Also note: **Prisma `Decimal` values are serialized as strings** (e.g. `"100.00"`), so run
money values through `Number(...)` / the helpers in `src/lib/format.js` before formatting.

Catalog rows and policy objects also carry a provider-defined `key` (e.g. `"PG2"`, or a
collision-suffixed `"PG2-2"`, and may be `null`). It is **display-only** and **read-through
from the provider** — the client must **never generate or fabricate** it. It's a direct field
on each catalog row (`GET /v1/catalog`) and a **top-level** field on each policy object
(`GET /v1/policies`, already resolved from the catalog — prefer the top-level `key`). The UI
renders it as a name prefix (e.g. `PG2 - Premium Gold 2024`) on the catalog page, on the
policy card heading on the dashboard, and on the main heading of the single policy detail page
(`/policies/:id`, preferring top-level `policy.key`, falling back to `policyCatalog.key`); use
`formatPlanName(key, name)` in `src/lib/format.js`,
which drops the prefix and separator entirely when `key` is null/absent/blank. Nested premium
and claim line items are never individually prefixed.

The one place snake_case *is* correct is **request bodies you send** to the API
(`policy_catalog_id`, `policy_id`, `amount_claimed`, `extend_months`). Responses = camelCase;
request payloads = snake_case. See `src/api/client.js` for the canonical mapping.

Responses are also wrapped in a `{ data: ... }` envelope; the API client unwraps it and
returns `data`.

heading: Deployment (Vercel) — don't break SPA routing
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## Deployment (Vercel) — don't break SPA routing
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## Deployment (Vercel) — don't break SPA routing

This repo deploys to **Vercel**. [`vercel.json`](vercel.json) contains a rewrite that serves
`index.html` for any non-asset path:

```json
{ "rewrites": [{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html" }] }
```

**Do not remove or weaken this rewrite.** Without it, direct navigation to (or a refresh of)
any client-side route — `/dashboard`, `/catalog`, `/policies/:id` — returns a 404 from Vercel,
because only `index.html` exists as a real static file; the routes live inside the JS bundle.

heading: Auth — Firebase, and a previously-fixed race condition
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## Auth — Firebase, and a previously-fixed race condition
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## Auth — Firebase, and a previously-fixed race condition

Auth is **Firebase Authentication (Email/Password)**, wrapped by `src/context/AuthContext.jsx`.
The ID token is attached as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every API call, and a `401`
from the API redirects to `/login`.

**If you touch `AuthContext` or `ProtectedRoute`, preserve the loading-flag pattern.** There
was a race condition where the app redirected to `/login` on refresh before Firebase's
`onAuthStateChanged` had resolved the session. The fix: `AuthContext` exposes a `loading`
flag (default `true`, set `false` only after the first `onAuthStateChanged` fires). Routing
decisions must check `loading` **before** acting on whether a user exists:

- while `loading` is `true` → render a spinner, **make no redirect decision**;
- only once `loading` is `false` **and** there is no user → redirect to `/login`.

Never redirect based solely on "is there a user right now" — that's what reintroduces the bug.

heading: Responsive nav bar — preserve the mobile layout
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-client` > ## Responsive nav bar — preserve the mobile layout

heading: Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api
text: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api

heading: Overview
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Overview
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Overview

`vkai-insurance-client-api` is the backend API for the **client side** of **VK AI Labs
Insurance**, a personal portfolio project. It powers the customer-facing web app
(`vkai-insurance-client`) and exposes the operations a policyholder needs: signing in,
browsing the policy catalog, enrolling in policies, paying premiums (virtual — no real money
moves), and filing claims.

It is one of four independent repositories in the ecosystem. This repo owns **only** the
client side; the provider side lives in a completely separate cloud (Azure) and is never
modified from here.

heading: Core responsibilities
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Core responsibilities
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Core responsibilities

1. **Customer authentication verification** — verifies Firebase-issued customer JWTs using the
   Firebase Admin SDK. The app does not mint tokens; it validates the `Authorization: Bearer`
   token on each customer request and resolves it to a local user record.
2. **Policy catalog** — serves a catalog of available policies. This catalog is a **cached,
   read-only** copy of the provider's catalog, kept fresh two ways: a **PUSH** from the provider
   (inbound `POST /v1/sync/catalog`, applied immediately) and a **PULL** fallback (refreshed from
   the provider API when the cache is stale). Both feed the same `policy_catalog` table via the
   same upsert. Each catalog entry also caches a provider-owned display **`key`** (see "Catalog
   key" below).
3. **Policy enrollments** — lets a customer enroll in a catalog policy, creating a local
   enrollment record that is then synced to the provider.
4. **Premium payments (virtual)** — records premium payments against a policy. Payments are
   virtual/simulated; no real payment processing occurs.
5. **Claims** — lets a customer file claims against their policies and track claim status.

heading: Data ownership — independent database
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Data ownership — independent database
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Data ownership — independent database

This API maintains its **own independent PostgreSQL database**. There is **no shared database
with the provider side, ever.** The two sides are separate systems in separate clouds and
communicate exclusively over HTTPS. Neither side reads or writes the other's tables.

The client database is the source of truth for: users, the cached policy catalog, enrollments
(policies), premiums, and claims.

heading: Cross-cloud sync model
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Cross-cloud sync model
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Cross-cloud sync model

Because the client and provider are independent systems with no shared storage, state is kept
consistent through **event-triggered HTTPS calls** in both directions.

heading: Standard envelope
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Cross-cloud sync model > ### Standard envelope
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Cross-cloud sync model > ### Standard envelope

Every sync call — outbound and inbound — carries a standard envelope:

```json
{
  "event_id": "<uuid>",
  "event_type": "<e.g. policy.enrolled | policy.renewed | premium.paid | claim.filed>",
  "occurred_at": "<ISO-8601 timestamp>",
  "source": "client",
  "payload": { "...event-specific fields..." }
}
```

The meaningful business fields always live inside `payload`; the surrounding keys are
transport/metadata. Inbound handlers must read from `payload`, not the envelope root.

heading: Reliability: retry + idempotency
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Cross-cloud sync model > ### Reliability: retry + idempotency
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Cross-cloud sync model > ### Reliability: retry + idempotency

The `policies`, `premiums`, and `claims` tables each carry three fields that make sync robust:

- **`sync_status`** — `pending` → `synced` → `failed`. A local write always succeeds first;
  sync is best-effort and never blocks the customer's request.
- **`sync_attempts`** — incremented on each failed attempt.
- **`event_id`** — the idempotency key sent on the outbound call, reused on every retry so the
  receiving side can dedupe.

A **node-cron background job runs every 5 minutes**, finds records that are `pending` or
`failed` with `sync_attempts < 5`, and retries them (reusing the same `event_id`). After 5
failed attempts a record stays `failed` for a future "sync issues" admin view to surface.

Inbound status updates are **idempotent**: if a record is already in the requested status, the
handler treats it as a no-op success, so replays are safe.

heading: Endpoint categories
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Endpoint categories
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Endpoint categories

The API has two distinct classes of endpoints with **different authentication schemes**:

heading: 1. Customer-authenticated routes (Firebase JWT)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 1. Customer-authenticated routes (Firebase JWT)
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 1. Customer-authenticated routes (Firebase JWT)

Called by the frontend on behalf of a signed-in customer. Protected by the Firebase auth
middleware (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`):

- **Catalog** — browse available policies (refreshed from the provider when stale).
- **Policies** — enroll, list the customer's own policies (with nested premiums/claims for the
  dashboard), and renew.
- **Premiums** — pay a premium against one of the customer's policies.
- **Claims** — file a claim and list the customer's claims.

Each customer route scopes data to the authenticated user — a customer can only see and act on
their own policies, premiums, and claims.

heading: 2. Inbound sync routes (shared secret, NOT customer JWTs)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 2. Inbound sync routes (shared secret, NOT customer JWTs)
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 2. Inbound sync routes (shared secret, NOT customer JWTs)

Called **by the provider side**, not by customers. These are protected by a **shared secret**
sent in the `X-VKAI-Sync-Key` header — **never** by a customer JWT. They let the provider push
authoritative changes back to the client. Requests with a missing or invalid sync key are
rejected with 401. Current inbound routes:

- `POST /v1/sync/policies/status` — provider pushes a policy status change (idempotent no-op if
  already in target status).
- `POST /v1/sync/claims/status` — provider pushes a claim status change (same pattern).
- `POST /v1/sync/catalog` — provider PUSHES a catalog create/edit/deactivate (VKAI-003, see
  "Push-based catalog sync" below).

heading: Catalog key (VKAI-002)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Catalog key (VKAI-002)
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Catalog key (VKAI-002)

The provider owns a display **`key`** on each catalog entry (e.g. `"PG2"`, or the
collision-suffixed `"PG2-2"`). As of VKAI-002 the provider's catalog-pull endpoint
(`GET /v1/catalog/policies`, the source this API refreshes its cache from) returns `key` on
every row.

Rules:

- **Cached, not owned.** The client stores `key` verbatim on each cached catalog row
  (`policy_catalog.key`, nullable). The client **never generates** a key — it only stores and
  echoes what the provider sends. On refresh, the existing upsert (matched on
  `provider_policy_id`) **updates** the row's `key` in place; no duplicates are created. `key` is
  nullable so pre-existing cached rows stay valid until the next refresh fills it in.
- **Display-only.** `key` is **not** a field on `policies`, `premiums`, or `claims`, and it is
  **not** part of any enrollment/premium/claim sync payload. It exists purely to label catalog
  entries in the UI.
- **Where it's exposed.**
  - `GET /v1/catalog` — each catalog row carries `key` (string or `null`) directly, since rows
    serialize straight from `policy_catalog`.
  - `GET /v1/policies` — each policy carries a top-level `key`, **looked up through the cached
    catalog relation** (`policyCatalog.key`) the policy already references — not stored on the
    policy. It degrades to `null` when the referenced catalog entry has no key yet (e.g. the cache
    hasn't been refreshed since the provider added keys). Nested `premiums` and `claims` do **not**
    get a `key`.
- **Force-refresh.** After the provider ships a catalog change, run
  `npm run catalog:refresh` (script: `scripts/refresh-catalog.js`) to pull immediately, bypassing
  the 15-minute staleness window, so already-cached rows pick up their `key` right away. See
  README / CLAUDE.md for the exact deploy command.

heading: Push-based catalog sync (VKAI-003)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Push-based catalog sync (VKAI-003)
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Push-based catalog sync (VKAI-003)

The catalog cache is kept fresh by **two complementary paths that both write the same
`policy_catalog` table through the same upsert** (`upsertCatalogItem` in
`src/services/catalogSync.js`):

- **PUSH (primary, immediate).** The provider calls the inbound route
  `POST /v1/sync/catalog` whenever a catalog entry is **created, edited, or deactivated**. This
  applies the change to the cache right away, instead of waiting for staleness.
- **PULL (fallback, unchanged).** The existing 15-minute stale-cache refresh from the provider's
  `GET /v1/catalog/policies` remains fully intact as a safety net (e.g. a missed push). VKAI-003
  is **additive** — it does not remove or weaken the pull.

Contract for `POST /v1/sync/catalog`:

- **Auth:** the shared-secret `X-VKAI-Sync-Key` header (same `syncAuth` middleware as every other
  inbound sync route). Missing/invalid key → 401. Not a customer/Firebase JWT.
- **Envelope:** the standard snake_case envelope `{ event_id, event_type, occurred_at, source,
  payload }`. `event_type` is `catalog.upserted` — a **single event type covers create, edit and
  deactivate**. Business fields are read from `payload`, never the envelope root.
- **Payload is camelCase** (unlike the snake_case status-sync payloads) and mirrors the pull
  response `GET /v1/catalog/policies` row **one-for-one**: `id`, `key`, `name`, `description`,
  `premiumAmount` (decimal-as-string), `coverageAmount` (decimal-as-string), `isActive`,
  `createdAt`.
- **Dedupe / idempotency:** upsert keyed on `payload.id` → `policy_catalog.provider_policy_id`
  (the business/dedupe key). A re-delivered or retried event never creates a duplicate row, and
  applying the same event twice yields the same final state. We do **not** separately record
  `event_id`, matching this repo's other inbound handlers, which rely on idempotent state rather
  than an event-log table.
- **Deactivation:** `isActive: false` is stored verbatim on `policy_catalog.is_active`. The
  customer-facing `GET /v1/catalog` filters to `isActive = true`, so a deactivated plan
  immediately disappears from the browse catalog. (Existing customer policies referencing a now
  deactivated catalog entry are unaffected — only the browse catalog is filtered.)

heading: Deployment
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Deployment
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Deployment

Production runs on a **GCP Compute Engine VM**. A **GitHub Actions** pipeline
(`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) **automatically deploys on every push to `main`**: it SSHes to
the VM, pulls the latest code, rebuilds the Docker containers, and verifies the API is healthy
via `/healthz`. See [README.md](README.md#deployment) for details and the required repo secrets.

heading: What this repo is
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## What this repo is
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## What this repo is

The backend API for the **client side** of "VK AI Labs Insurance" (a personal portfolio
project). It serves the `vkai-insurance-client` frontend and handles customer auth verification
(Firebase Admin SDK), the cached policy catalog, policy enrollments, virtual premium payments,
and claims. It owns its **own independent Postgres database** — there is **no shared database**
with the provider side, ever. It syncs with the provider API (Azure) over HTTPS using a standard
envelope `{ event_id, event_type, occurred_at, source, payload }`. See
[BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md](BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md) for the full picture and
[README.md](README.md) for setup.

heading: Naming conventions
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Naming conventions
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## Naming conventions

- **Env vars**: prefix everything with `VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_*` (the provider base URL,
  `VKAI_INSURANCE_PROVIDER_API_BASE_URL`, is the one deliberate exception — it names the other
  system).
- **Database columns**: `snake_case`, tables plural (`policy_catalog`, `policies`, …).
- **Prisma model fields**: `camelCase`, mapped to snake_case columns via `@map`.
- **JSON API responses are camelCase, not snake_case** — they serialize Prisma objects directly.
  Inbound request payloads from the provider, however, use snake_case inside `payload` (e.g.
  `client_policy_id`, `provider_policy_id`). Don't assume one casing everywhere; check the
  direction of the data.

### CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way)

heading: 1. docker-compose.yml lists env vars EXPLICITLY — it does not load .env
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 1. docker-compose.yml lists env vars EXPLICITLY — it does not load .env
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 1. docker-compose.yml lists env vars EXPLICITLY — it does not load .env

The `api` service enumerates each environment variable individually; it does **not** bulk-load
the `.env` file. **Any new env var added to `.env.example` and the app code MUST also be added
to the `api` service's `environment:` list in `docker-compose.yml`**, or the running container
silently never receives it (the app falls back to a default or breaks with no obvious error —
this is exactly how CORS broke once). **Always cross-check all three when adding a var:**
`.env.example`, the app code that reads it, and `docker-compose.yml`.

heading: 2. A manual fix on a deployed VM is LOCAL-ONLY until committed
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 2. A manual fix on a deployed VM is LOCAL-ONLY until committed
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 2. A manual fix on a deployed VM is LOCAL-ONLY until committed

Any change made directly on a deployed VM (editing a file over `ssh`/`nano`, etc.) lives only on
that VM's disk and is **invisible to git**. It will be lost or overwritten and is not part of the
codebase until it is explicitly committed and pushed through the normal
`dev` → PR → `main` workflow. **Never leave a fix living only on a VM.** Port it back into the
repo.

heading: 3. Inbound sync routes MUST unwrap the standard envelope
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 3. Inbound sync routes MUST unwrap the standard envelope
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 3. Inbound sync routes MUST unwrap the standard envelope

The provider wraps every outbound call in `{ event_id, event_type, occurred_at, source,
payload }`. Inbound handlers in `src/routes/sync.js` must read business fields from
**`req.body.payload`**, not `req.body` directly. Reading them off the root was a real bug that
made every inbound status sync fail with 400. The unwrap helper handles both enveloped and flat
bodies defensively — keep it; don't reintroduce the bug.

heading: 4. Firebase Admin private key formatting
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 4. Firebase Admin private key formatting
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 4. Firebase Admin private key formatting

`VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY` in `.env` must stay on **one line, quoted, with
literal `\n` text** (the app converts `\n` back into real newlines at load time). **Never let an
editor "clean up" the key into real multi-line breaks** — that corrupts the key and Firebase
initialization fails.

heading: 5. Local cross-container networking
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 5. Local cross-container networking
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 5. Local cross-container networking

When testing against a sibling repo's API running in **its own** Docker Compose project locally,
use `http://host.docker.internal:<port>` — **not** `localhost`. Inside a container `localhost`
refers to the container itself, so `localhost:<port>` will not reach a service in another compose
project.

heading: 6. CI/CD deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions → GCP VM)
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 6. CI/CD deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions → GCP VM)
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 6. CI/CD deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions → GCP VM)

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` auto-deploys to the production GCP VM on every push to `main`
(SSH via `appleboy/ssh-action`: `git pull`, `docker compose up --build -d`, health check).
Two things were learned the hard way building it:

- **Use absolute paths in the deploy script, NOT `~`.** `~` does **not** reliably expand in this
  SSH action's non-interactive shell, causing `No such file or directory` even when the path is
  correct. Use the full path, e.g. `/home/vibhavkulshrestha/vkai-insurance-client-api`.
- **The health check needs a real wait + retry, not an immediate single curl.** Postgres
  healthcheck + Prisma migration + API startup takes longer than a few seconds. The workflow
  sleeps **20s** then retries the `/healthz` curl **5 times, 5s apart** before failing. A single
  immediate check produces false 502 failures on a deploy that actually succeeded.

Requires these **GitHub repo secrets**: `DEPLOY_HOST`, `DEPLOY_USER`, `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY`.

heading: 7. Catalog `key` is display-only — never put it on policies/premiums/claims (VKAI-002)
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 7. Catalog `key` is display-only — never put it on policies/premiums/claims (VKAI-002)
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 7. Catalog `key` is display-only — never put it on policies/premiums/claims (VKAI-002)

The provider owns a display `key` per catalog entry. This API **caches** it on
`policy_catalog.key` (nullable) — filled in from the provider's `GET /v1/catalog/policies` pull,
matched/updated on `provider_policy_id`. **The client never generates a key**; it only stores/echoes
what the provider sends.

- It is **NOT** a column on `policies`, `premiums`, or `claims`, and **NOT** in any sync payload.
  Don't add it there.
- `GET /v1/catalog` exposes `key` directly on each row (rows serialize from `policy_catalog`).
- `GET /v1/policies` exposes a top-level `key` per policy **read through the `policyCatalog`
  relation** (not a policy column), degrading to `null` when the catalog entry has no key yet.
  Nested premiums/claims must NOT carry a key.
- **Force-refresh** (bypass the 15-min staleness window) with `npm run catalog:refresh`
  (`scripts/refresh-catalog.js`), which calls `refreshCatalogFromProvider()` directly. Run it at
  deploy where the provider API is reachable, e.g. `docker compose exec api npm run catalog:refresh`.

heading: 8. Catalog is push+pull; the push payload is camelCase (VKAI-003)
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 8. Catalog is push+pull; the push payload is camelCase (VKAI-003)
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for vkai-insurance-client-api > ## CRITICAL gotchas (learned the hard way) > ### 8. Catalog is push+pull; the push payload is camelCase (VKAI-003)

The provider now **PUSHES** catalog create/edit/deactivate to `POST /v1/sync/catalog`
immediately, in addition to the existing stale-cache **PULL** fallback. Both paths write the
same `policy_catalog` table through the **same** `upsertCatalogItem()` in
`src/services/catalogSync.js` — keep it that way; don't fork the mapping.

- **The push payload is camelCase**, unlike the snake_case status-sync payloads on the other
  inbound routes. It mirrors the pull's `GET /v1/catalog/policies` row one-for-one (`id`, `key`,
  `name`, `description`, `premiumAmount`, `coverageAmount`, `isActive`, `createdAt`). Don't
  snake_case it.
- **Dedupe/upsert on `payload.id` → `provider_policy_id`** (the business key). No separate
  `event_id` log — the other inbound handlers dedupe via idempotent state, not an event table, so
  this route follows suit. Upsert-on-id makes retries/redeliveries a no-op-equivalent.
- **`isActive: false` = deactivation.** It's stored verbatim, and `GET /v1/catalog` filters
  `isActive: true` so a deactivated plan drops out of the browse catalog. Whenever the pull's
  mapping used to assume "always active" — it no longer can; the push can flip a row inactive.
- Guarded by the same `syncAuth` (`X-VKAI-Sync-Key`) middleware as the other `/v1/sync/*` routes;
  no new env var was needed.

heading: Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal)
text: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal)

heading: Overview
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Overview
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Overview

The **Provider Portal** is the ops-facing frontend of **VK AI Labs Insurance**, a personal
portfolio project. It is used by insurance **provider staff** — not by customers — to
review and act on the insurance records that flow in from the customer-facing side of the
platform.

The portal is built entirely on **Azure** and is paired with its own backend,
`vkai-insurance-provider-api`. It is **fully independent** from the customer-facing "client
side," which runs on **GCP** with its own frontend, backend, and database. The two sides
**share no database**; they exchange data only over **HTTPS** (cross-cloud sync). This
portal has no direct knowledge of the GCP side beyond the records that sync in.

heading: Users & authentication
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Users & authentication
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Users & authentication

All ops users sign in with **Entra ID (Azure AD)** using their **own individual login** —
there is **never a shared password**. Individual logins are a hard requirement so that
every action (activating an enrollment, approving a claim, etc.) is attributable to a
specific person for **audit-trail** purposes.

Authorization is enforced **server-side by the API**. The frontend reads the Entra ID
**groups claim** to tailor the UI (show/hide buttons) as a convenience only — it is not the
security boundary.

heading: Roles
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Roles
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Roles

There are two ops roles, defined by Entra ID security-group membership. A user in **both**
groups is treated as an **Approver** (Approver is a superset of Reviewer).

heading: Reviewer
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Roles > ### Reviewer
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Roles > ### Reviewer

- View all records (dashboard, catalog, enrollments, claims, premiums, sync issues).
- Move a claim from **Submitted → Under Review**.

heading: Approver
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Roles > ### Approver
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Roles > ### Approver

Everything a Reviewer can do, **plus**:

- **Approve** / **reject** claims.
- **Mark** approved claims **as paid**.
- **Manage the policy catalog** — create, edit, and deactivate plans.
- **Activate** pending enrollments.

### Core pages

heading: Dashboard
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Dashboard
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Dashboard

At-a-glance **summary counts**: pending enrollments, claims broken down by status, and the
number of outstanding sync issues. Entry point after sign-in.

heading: Catalog
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Catalog
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Catalog

Where the provider **defines the insurance plans** (name, description, premium amount,
coverage amount). The catalog is the **source of truth** for plans: the client (GCP) side
**caches a read-only copy** of it, and customers enroll in those plans over there.

- **Both roles:** view plans.
- **Approver only:** add, edit, and deactivate plans.

Every catalog entry has an auto-generated, **locked "key"**. The key is the first character
of each whitespace-separated token of the plan name, uppercased (e.g. `Premium Gold 2024`
→ `PG2`), with a `-2` / `-3` … suffix appended on collision so keys stay unique. The key is
**generated after the plan is saved** — it is not chosen by the user. On the **Add Plan**
screen the Key field appears **below Name**, is **non-editable**, and is populated once the
plan has been saved. In the catalog list the key is shown as a **prefix to the plan name**
(e.g. `PG2 - Premium Gold 2024`).

heading: Enrollments
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Enrollments
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Enrollments

The **pending-enrollment queue** — enrollment requests that have synced in from the client
side and are awaiting provider action.

- **Both roles:** view the queue.
- **Approver only:** **activate** an enrollment (the activation is then synced back to the
  client side).

heading: Claims
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Claims
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Claims

Claims move through a status workflow:

```
Submitted → Under Review → Approved  → Paid
                         ↘ Rejected
```

- **Move to Under Review** (Submitted → Under Review): Reviewer **or** Approver.
- **Approve** / **Reject**: Approver only.
- **Mark as Paid** (from Approved): Approver only.

The gating is **flexible**: an Approver may approve or reject a claim directly without a
Reviewer having moved it to Under Review first — there is no strict Reviewer-first
requirement. Each transition is synced back to the client side.

heading: Premiums
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Premiums
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Premiums

**View-only** payment history. No actions — ops staff can see premium payments that have
been recorded but do not modify them here.

The premiums table's **first (left-most) column is "Policy Name"**, populated from the API's
`policyName` field on each premium (the resolved plan catalog name). When `policyName` is
`null`, absent, or blank, the cell renders the literal text **"Unknown plan"** — the
frontend never fabricates or derives a plan name. The remaining columns (Policy ref, Amount,
Paid at, Sync status) follow unchanged.

heading: Sync Issues
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Sync Issues
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Core pages > ### Sync Issues

Visibility into cross-cloud syncs that have **permanently failed**. Because the provider and
client sides share no database and rely on HTTPS sync, this page surfaces records
(policies, premiums, claims) whose sync to the client side ultimately failed, so ops staff
are aware of them. Read-only — it is a visibility screen, not a retry console.

heading: Out of scope
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Out of scope
text:
# Business Requirements — VK AI Labs Insurance (Provider Portal) > ## Out of scope

- No customer-facing functionality (that lives entirely on the independent GCP client side).
- No shared database with the client side — integration is HTTPS sync only.
- No payment-gateway integration; premiums are recorded history, not processed here.
