heading: Authentication — CRITICAL, do not "simplify"
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — Project context for `vkai-insurance-provider` > ## Authentication — CRITICAL, do not "simplify"
text:
# CLAUDE.md — Project context for `vkai-insurance-provider` > ## Authentication — CRITICAL, do not "simplify"

Auth uses MSAL **`loginRedirect`, NOT `loginPopup`**, with a **dedicated redirect route
`/auth/callback`**. This structure is a hard-won fix — **do not revert to popup-based login
or a bare-origin redirect URI.**

Root-cause history (why it is the way it is):

1. **`loginPopup` broke on mobile Safari** — React Router stripped the auth response hash
   inside the popup window before MSAL could read it (`hash_empty_error`). Fixed by
   switching to `loginRedirect` everywhere (login, token-refresh fallback, logout).
2. **A bare-origin `redirectUri` then broke on desktop** — Microsoft redirected back to
   `/`, and the root route (`<Navigate to="/dashboard">`) immediately navigated away,
   stripping the `#code=...` hash before `handleRedirectPromise` could read it → silent,
   errorless failure back to `/login`. Fixed with a **dedicated `/auth/callback` route** that
   nothing else navigates away from.
3. **Routing races** were fixed by making routing decisions **`inProgress`-aware**:
   `ProtectedRoute`, `LoginPage`, and `AuthCallbackPage` all wait for
   `inProgress === InteractionStatus.None` (from `@azure/msal-browser`) before deciding
   authenticated vs. not — never act on a transient `isAuthenticated === false` mid-redirect.

If you touch auth/routing, understand all three points above first. Do not collapse
`/auth/callback` or the `inProgress` gating.

heading: Overview
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Overview
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Overview

This is the backend API for the **provider / ops side** of *VK AI Labs Insurance*, a
personal portfolio project. It is the system of record for the insurance operations team and
serves the provider frontend (`vkai-insurance-provider`). It runs on **Azure**.

The platform is split across two fully independent clouds that never share a database:

- **Provider side (Azure)** — *this repo* and its frontend. Ops staff (Reviewers/Approvers)
  manage the plan catalog and work claims here.
- **Client side (GCP)** — `vkai-insurance-client` + `vkai-insurance-client-api`. Policy
  holders enroll, pay premiums, and file claims there.

The two sides stay consistent by exchanging **event-enveloped HTTPS sync calls** — there is
no shared storage, no cross-cloud database link, and no shared runtime. Each side owns its
own Postgres instance.

heading: Responsibilities
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Responsibilities
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Responsibilities

This API owns the following provider-side concerns:

1. **Ops user authentication** — verifies Entra ID (Azure AD) JWTs on every ops request and
   upserts an `ops_users` record from the token claims. Group membership maps to an internal
   role (**Reviewer** or **Approver**).
2. **Policy catalog** — the **source of truth** for insurance plans. The client side only
   caches a read-only copy. It **pulls** that copy periodically from this API
   (`GET /v1/catalog/policies`) **and** — as of **VKAI-003** — receives an immediate
   **push** whenever a plan is created or edited/deactivated here, so its cache reflects with
   no wait. The pull remains the fallback; the push is best-effort with retry (see the
   outbound sync table below). Plans are created and edited/deactivated here.

   - **Auto-generated, locked plan key.** Every policy catalog entry carries a short `key`,
     generated **server-side on plan creation**. It is derived from the plan name by taking
     the **first character of each whitespace-separated token, uppercased, and concatenated**
     (e.g. `"Premium Gold 2024"` → `"PG2"`). On collision the key is made unique with a
     dash-numeric suffix (`"-2"`, `"-3"`, …). The key is **non-editable** once created and is
     displayed as a **prefix to the plan name** wherever the catalog is shown. As of
     **VKAI-002**, `key` is part of the cross-cloud catalog payload the client caches (see
     `GET /v1/catalog/policies` below); it is no longer provider-only.
3. **Enrollment processing** — enrollment instances originate on the client side and are
   mirrored into this API's `policies` table via inbound sync. Ops activates them, which
   pushes the new status back to the client.
4. **Premium records** — premium payments are recorded on the client side and pushed here
   for visibility. They are stored passively; no outbound push back is required.

   - **`policyName` enrichment (VKAI-004).** `GET /v1/premiums` returns each premium enriched
     with a `policyName` field (string, or `null`), resolved **entirely from provider-local
     data** via the relational join `premium -> policy -> policyCatalog` (the catalog `name`).
     No cross-cloud call is made — the provider owns the catalog as source of truth. When the
     name can't be resolved (no linked policy, or no matching catalog row) `policyName` is
     `null` and the frontend renders the literal "Unknown plan". A deactivated-but-present plan
     (`isActive=false`) still has a catalog row and resolves to its real name normally — that is
     not a fallback case. This is read-only enrichment: no schema, sync-payload, or auth change.
5. **Claims workflow** — the full claim lifecycle worked by ops:
   `Submitted → Under Review → Approved / Rejected → Paid`. Each transition is role-gated and
   pushes the resulting status back to the client side.

heading: Data ownership & cross-cloud model
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Data ownership & cross-cloud model
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Data ownership & cross-cloud model

- This API maintains its **own independent Postgres database**, entirely separate from the
  client side's. No foreign keys cross the cloud boundary — client-side references are
  stored as opaque values (`client_user_ref`, `client_policy_id`, `client_claim_id`).
- Synchronization uses the **same event-enveloped pattern documented on the client-api
  side**. Every sync message is wrapped in a standard envelope:

  ```json
  {
    "event_id": "<uuid>",
    "event_type": "policy.activated",
    "occurred_at": "<iso-8601>",
    "source": "provider",
    "payload": { }
  }
  ```

- Reliability is built into every synced table via three fields — `sync_status`
  (`pending` / `synced` / `failed`), `sync_attempts`, and `event_id`:
  - **Idempotency** — inbound routes dedupe on `event_id` (or the business key
    `client_policy_id` / `client_claim_id`), so a retried delivery never creates a duplicate
    row.
  - **Retry** — a background job (every 5 minutes) re-pushes outbound rows still in
    `pending`/`failed` with `sync_attempts < 5`, reusing the stored `event_id` so the far
    side can dedupe.
  - **Resilience** — an ops action always succeeds locally even if its outbound sync push
    fails; the push is simply marked `failed` and retried later.

### Endpoint categories

heading: 1. Ops-authenticated routes (`Authorization: Bearer <Entra ID JWT>`)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 1. Ops-authenticated routes (`Authorization: Bearer <Entra ID JWT>`)
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 1. Ops-authenticated routes (`Authorization: Bearer <Entra ID JWT>`)

Consumed by the provider frontend. Every request must carry a valid Entra ID token; the auth
middleware verifies it and attaches the resolved `ops_users` record. Sensitive actions are
**role-gated** via a `requireRole('Approver')` helper.

| Route | Access | Purpose |
| ----- | ------ | ------- |
| `GET /v1/policy-catalog` | any ops user | List plans |
| `POST /v1/policy-catalog` | **Approver** | Create a plan |
| `PATCH /v1/policy-catalog/:id` | **Approver** | Edit / deactivate a plan |
| `GET /v1/policies` | any ops user | List enrollments (`?status=pending` queue) |
| `POST /v1/policies/:id/activate` | **Approver** | Activate → push status to client |
| `GET /v1/premiums` | any ops user | View premium records (each row enriched with `policyName`, see note below) |
| `GET /v1/claims` | any ops user | List claims (`?status=` filter) |
| `POST /v1/claims/:id/review` | Reviewer / Approver | → Under Review, push status |
| `POST /v1/claims/:id/approve` | **Approver** | → Approved, push status |
| `POST /v1/claims/:id/reject` | **Approver** | → Rejected, push status |
| `POST /v1/claims/:id/mark-paid` | **Approver** | → Paid (only from Approved), push status |
| `GET /v1/sync-issues` | any ops user | Rows where `sync_status = failed` |

> A Reviewer touching a claim before an Approver acts is **not** enforced — any Approver may
> act on a claim regardless of its review history (deliberate scope decision).

heading: 2. Cross-cloud routes (`X-VKAI-Sync-Key` shared secret)
breadcrumb: # Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 2. Cross-cloud routes (`X-VKAI-Sync-Key` shared secret)
text:
# Business Requirements — vkai-insurance-provider-api > ## Endpoint categories > ### 2. Cross-cloud routes (`X-VKAI-Sync-Key` shared secret)

**Not** protected by the ops JWT. These are the machine-to-machine boundary between the two
clouds, protected instead by a shared secret header. The client side calls **into** these,
and this API's own outbound sync calls back **into** the client side's equivalent routes
using the same key.

| Route | Direction | Purpose |
| ----- | --------- | ------- |
| `GET /v1/catalog/policies` | client **pulls** from provider | Active catalog rows to cache (includes `key` as of VKAI-002) |
| `POST /v1/sync/policies` | client **pushes** to provider | New enrollment → `policies` (pending) |
| `POST /v1/sync/premiums` | client **pushes** to provider | Premium payment → `premiums` |
| `POST /v1/sync/claims` | client **pushes** to provider | New claim → `claims` (Submitted) |

Outbound (provider → client), triggered by ops actions:

| Called after | Target on client side | Event type |
| ------------ | --------------------- | ---------- |
| Policy activation | `POST /v1/sync/policies/status` | `policy.activated` |
| Any claim status change | `POST /v1/sync/claims/status` | `claim.<status>` |
| Catalog create or edit/deactivate | `POST /v1/sync/catalog` | `catalog.upserted` |

The **catalog push** (VKAI-003) uses the same reliability trio as the other outbound rows:
`sync_status` / `sync_attempts` / `event_id` now live on `policy_catalog` too, the 5-minute
retry job re-pushes any catalog row not confirmed `synced`, and the ops create/edit always
succeeds locally even if the push fails. The payload is the full catalog row the client
upserts into its cache — camelCase, mirroring the `GET /v1/catalog/policies` pull shape:
`{ id, key, name, description, premiumAmount, coverageAmount, isActive, createdAt }`. The
client **dedupes/upserts on `payload.id`** (the provider catalog UUID). A deactivation is
pushed as a normal `catalog.upserted` with `isActive: false`.

# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api`

Context for future Claude Code sessions working in this repo. Read this before making

heading: What this repo is
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## What this repo is
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## What this repo is

The backend API for the **provider / ops side** of *VK AI Labs Insurance* (Azure). It serves
the `vkai-insurance-provider` frontend and owns the policy catalog, enrollments, premiums,
and the claims workflow. It has its **own Postgres database** and syncs with the GCP client
side over HTTPS with an event envelope. See [BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md](BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md)
for the full domain model and [README.md](README.md) for setup.

heading: Naming conventions
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## Naming conventions
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## Naming conventions

- **Env vars:** prefix everything with `VKAI_INSURANCE_PROVIDER_API_*` (the one exception is
  `VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL`, shared across repos).
- **Prisma model fields & JSON responses:** `camelCase` (same as the client-api side). The
  Prisma schema maps camelCase fields to `snake_case`, plural DB tables via `@map` / `@@map`;
  API request/response bodies stay camelCase.
- **API routes:** `/v1/<resource>`, kebab-case, plural nouns.

### CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these

heading: Entra ID (Azure AD) auth
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Entra ID (Azure AD) auth
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Entra ID (Azure AD) auth

- **Audience must accept BOTH forms.** Azure may issue tokens with an `aud` of either the
  bare client ID *or* the `api://<client-id>` URI form, depending on how the token was
  requested (the latter when the exposed `access_as_user` scope is used). The verification in
  [src/middleware/entraAuth.js](src/middleware/entraAuth.js) passes an **array** to
  `jsonwebtoken`'s `audience` option: `[clientId, "api://" + clientId]`. **Never hardcode a
  single expected audience value** — doing so breaks every request with a
  `jwt audience invalid` error.
- **Token version must be pinned to v2.** The app registration must set
  `requestedAccessTokenVersion: 2` in the **new Microsoft Graph app manifest**. Do *not* use
  the old, deprecating AAD Graph manifest — it uses a differently-named field, and without
  the v2 pin the issued tokens carry the wrong issuer format (the issuer check expects
  `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`). This is a Portal step, not code, but
  the code depends on it.

heading: Prisma + Docker on Alpine
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Prisma + Docker on Alpine
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Prisma + Docker on Alpine

- The [Dockerfile](Dockerfile) **pins Prisma `binaryTargets`** (in
  [prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma): `native`, `linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x`,
  `linux-musl-arm64-openssl-3.0.x`) **and installs `openssl` in the build stage**. This
  avoids an OpenSSL version mismatch on Alpine where Prisma otherwise generates a
  `1.1.x` engine but the runtime needs `3.0.x`, crashing the container on boot with
  "Prisma Client could not locate the Query Engine". **Do not remove either of these** if you
  touch the Dockerfile or schema generator block.

heading: Deployed-VM fixes are invisible to git
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Deployed-VM fixes are invisible to git
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Deployed-VM fixes are invisible to git

- Any fix made **directly on a deployed VM** (via `nano`/`ssh`) is **LOCAL-ONLY** and
  invisible to git. It will be silently lost on the next deploy and is not reproducible.

heading: Sync envelope
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Sync envelope
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Sync envelope

- Outbound and inbound sync routes must wrap/unwrap the standard envelope
  `{ event_id, event_type, occurred_at, source, payload }`. Outbound wrapping lives in
  [src/services/clientSync.js](src/services/clientSync.js); inbound unwrapping uses the
  `unwrap()` helper in [src/routes/crossCloud.js](src/routes/crossCloud.js) (which also
  tolerates a flat body). **Preserve this pattern in any new sync route** — read
  `event_id`/`payload` via `unwrap()`, never assume a flat body.

heading: Outbound catalog push (VKAI-003)
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Outbound catalog push (VKAI-003)
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Outbound catalog push (VKAI-003)

- The **policy catalog is the source of truth** and was originally not an outbound-synced
  table. VKAI-003 added the reliability trio (`sync_status` / `sync_attempts` / `event_id`,
  see the `*_add_policy_catalog_sync` migration) to `policy_catalog` and pushes every
  create/edit to the client's `POST /v1/sync/catalog`. Reuse this same mechanism for any
  future catalog-affecting sync — **don't** invent a parallel outbox.
- **Migration backfills existing rows to `sync_status = 'synced'`** on purpose: they predate
  push-sync and are already in the client cache via the pull, so this stops the 5-min retry
  sweep from re-pushing the entire pre-existing catalog on first deploy.
- **The catalog push payload is camelCase**, unlike the other outbound payloads
  (`client_claim_id` etc. are snake_case). This is deliberate: the catalog payload mirrors the
  `GET /v1/catalog/policies` pull response one-for-one, because the client feeds the SAME
  cached-catalog copy from both the pull and the push. The envelope itself stays snake_case.
  The shared shape lives in [src/lib/catalogSync.js](src/lib/catalogSync.js) so the route push
  and the cron retry can't drift. Client dedupes/upserts on `payload.id` (provider catalog UUID).
- **Event type is `catalog.upserted`** (single event covers create, edit, and deactivate) so
  the client handler is a plain upsert with no branching; a deactivate is just `isActive:false`.

heading: Policy catalog `key` — generation + deliberate cross-cloud exclusion
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Policy catalog `key` — generation + deliberate cross-cloud exclusion
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Policy catalog `key` — generation + deliberate cross-cloud exclusion

- **Generation algorithm (keep in lockstep).** Each policy catalog entry has an
  auto-generated `key`: split the plan name on whitespace, take the **first character of each
  token uppercased**, and concatenate (`"Premium Gold 2024"` → `"PG2"`; a numeric token
  contributes its first digit). Uniqueness is enforced with a **readable dash-numeric suffix
  starting at 2** on collision (`"PG2"` → `"PG2-2"` → `"PG2-3"` …). The shared helpers live in
  [src/lib/policyKey.js](src/lib/policyKey.js): `derivePolicyKey` (pure derivation) and
  `makeUniquePolicyKey` (DB-checked uniqueness). This algorithm is duplicated in the SQL
  backfill of the `*_add_policy_catalog_key` migration — **any change must update both.**
- **`key` IS included in the cross-cloud `GET /v1/catalog/policies`** (the client cache
  pull) via the explicit Prisma `select` in
  [src/routes/crossCloud.js](src/routes/crossCloud.js). **(SUPERSEDED by VKAI-002.)** VKAI-001
  originally excluded `key` from this route so it would not leak to the client side; VKAI-002
  reversed that decision and `key` now flows to the client on purpose. **Keep the explicit
  `select`** — do not switch it back to a bare `findMany` or a wildcard select. The response
  shape stays intentional; `key` is just one of the selected fields.
- **`key` DOES appear on the ops-authenticated `GET /v1/policies`** because that route nests
  the full `policyCatalog` object (`include: { policyCatalog: true }`). This is
  provider-internal and intentional — **not** a leak, since that route is behind the Entra ID
  ops JWT.

heading: Env vars must be in TWO places
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Env vars must be in TWO places
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### Env vars must be in TWO places

- CORS is configured via `VKAI_INSURANCE_PROVIDER_API_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` and was included in
  [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)'s explicit `environment:` list **from the start**
  (a deliberate fix for an earlier client-side gotcha where an env var was missing at
  runtime). When adding **any** new env var, add it to **BOTH**
  [.env.example](.env.example) **AND** the `api` service's `environment:` block in
  `docker-compose.yml` — otherwise it will be silently missing inside the container.

heading: CI/CD deploy pipeline (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
breadcrumb: # CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### CI/CD deploy pipeline (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
text:
# CLAUDE.md — project context for `vkai-insurance-provider-api` > ## CRITICAL gotchas — do not reintroduce these > ### CI/CD deploy pipeline (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)

Pushing to **`main`** auto-deploys to the production Azure VM via GitHub Actions
(`appleboy/ssh-action`). Hard-won gotchas from building this pipeline:

- **Use absolute paths, never `~`.** The deploy script `cd`s to
  `/home/vkaiadmin/vkai-insurance-provider-api` — **not** `~/vkai-insurance-provider-api`.
  Tilde does **not** reliably expand in this SSH action's non-interactive shell, so a `~`
  path silently lands in the wrong place and the deploy fails confusingly.
- **The health check needs a real wait + retry loop.** Postgres healthcheck + Prisma
  `migrate deploy` + API startup takes longer than a few seconds, so a single immediate
  `curl` races the boot and false-fails. The script waits **20s**, then retries the `/health`
  poll **5 times, 5s apart**, before giving up. Do not collapse this back to one early check.
- **Required per-repo secrets:** `DEPLOY_HOST`, `DEPLOY_USER`, `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY`. These are
  **this repo's own** secrets — **do NOT copy-paste them from the sibling client-api repo's
  values.** That mix-up happened once during setup (wrong host/key) and caused confusing
  early failures. Each repo deploys to its own VM with its own key.

# VK AI Labs — Naming Convention & Ecosystem Governance Guide

**Owner:** Vibhav Kulshrestha
**Purpose:** Single source of truth for naming, structure, and account conventions across a personal AI/Cloud/DevOps engineering demo ecosystem.
**Status:** Draft v1.0 — living document, refine as the build progresses.

text:
# VK AI Labs — Naming Convention & Ecosystem Governance Guide > ## 1. Master Brand

| Item | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Master Brand Name** | **VK AI Labs** (keep it — already anchored in your Gmail and Jira, changing now creates rework across every downstream system) |
| **Short Code (all-caps, used in Jira keys, prefixes)** | `VKAI` |
| **Slug (lowercase, used in URLs/repos/resources)** | `vkailabs` (no hyphen) — use this as your canonical slug everywhere technical. Use `vk-ai-labs` only where the platform *forces* hyphenation and disallows a contiguous domain-like slug (rare). |
| **Legal/Display Name** | VK AI Labs |
| **Full Formal Name (decks, docs headers)** | VK AI Labs — Engineering & AI Platform |

**Why keep "VK AI Labs":** it's short, personal-brand-forward (VK = your initials, instantly explains itself in interviews), and already live in 2 systems. Changing it now would fragment your Gmail handle, Jira site, and any muscle memory you build. If you ever want an alternate for a *specific* sub-venture (e.g., a public SaaS spin-off), you can layer a product name under the VK AI Labs umbrella later (see §3).

**Alternate names, only if you want a change (not recommended given Jira/Gmail already exist):**
- Kulshrestha Labs / KulTech Labs
- Vibhav.ai
- VKE — VK Engineering

heading: 3. Naming Grammar (the meta-rule everything below follows)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Naming Convention & Ecosystem Governance Guide > ## 3. Naming Grammar (the meta-rule everything below follows)
text:
# VK AI Labs — Naming Convention & Ecosystem Governance Guide > ## 3. Naming Grammar (the meta-rule everything below follows)

Define **once**, apply everywhere so a stranger (interviewer/client) can predict a name without seeing it:

```
<brand>-<domain/component>-<subcomponent>-<qualifier>
```

- **kebab-case** → repos, domains, subdomains, K8s resources, Docker images, folders
- **PascalCase** → .NET solutions/projects, NuGet packages, C# namespaces
- **camelCase** → variables, JSON keys, JS/TS identifiers
- **UPPER_SNAKE_CASE** → environment variables, constants
- **lowercase.dotted** → Java-style packages (if ever used)
- Always prefix internal artifacts with `vkai` — this is your "namespace" the same way a company uses its ticker.

| `mcp/` | MCP server implementations, tool manifests |
| `evaluations/` | Eval harnesses, golden datasets, scoring rubrics |
| `benchmarks/` | Latency/cost/accuracy benchmark results, tracked over time |
| `templates/` | Reusable prompt/agent/eval scaffolds |
| `fine-tuning/` *(add)* | If you ever fine-tune/distill models, keep configs + datasets here |
| `model-registry/` *(add)* | Track which model/version powers which agent, with changelog |

heading: 27. Additional Items You May Be Missing

text:

- **Postman/Bruno collection naming:** `VKAI - Core API - <Env>.postman_collection.json`.
- **Changelogs:** `CHANGELOG.md` per repo, Keep-a-Changelog format.

heading: VK AI Labs Insurance — AI Concepts Inventory (v1)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — AI Concepts Inventory (v1)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — AI Concepts Inventory (v1)

Assessment of which AI/GenAI concepts have actually been used (vs. only planned/named) in the VK AI Labs Insurance E2E Engineering Platform, based on `vkai-insurance-setup-log.md` and other project docs.

| # | Keyword | What it does (one-liner) | Used in Project? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agentic AI | AI that plans and takes multi-step actions autonomously, not just answers | **Yes** | `agent-vkai-master` + subagents: read docs, plan, code, commit, push — without step-by-step hand-holding |
| 2 | GenAI | Umbrella term for AI that generates content (code, text, docs) | **Yes** | Entire platform — code, docs, diagrams, test packs all AI-generated |
| 3 | LLM | The underlying language model doing the reasoning/generation | **Yes** | Claude (Sonnet) powering Claude Code + Claude.ai sessions throughout |
| 4 | RAG | Retrieving relevant docs to ground a response before generating | **Partially** | Claude.ai Project knowledge search over your mounted `.md` docs — that's retrieval-augmented, but no real pipeline (no embeddings/vector DB) built |
| 5 | Cowork | Anthropic's agentic desktop app for non-dev knowledge work | **No** | Not used — your workflow is Claude Code + Claude.ai Project |
| 6 | MCP | Protocol letting Claude call external tools/services directly | **Yes** | Atlassian Rovo MCP (real Jira Test Case + Story publishing), draw.io MCP (architecture diagrams) |
| 7 | Embedding | Converting text into vector representations for similarity search | **No** | Only listed as a future folder (`/ai/embeddings`) in naming conventions — never built |
| 8 | Context Engineering / Window | Deliberately shaping what info the model has at each step | **Yes** | `CLAUDE.md` per repo, fresh context passed explicitly to each subagent invocation (no shared memory) |
| 9 | Guardrails | Constraints that limit what an agent is allowed to do | **Yes** | `agent-vkai-jira-update` locked to `Read/Bash/Grep/Glob` (no Write/Edit); subagents scoped to their own repo only |
| 10 | Tokenisation | Breaking text into model-processable units | **No** | Never engineered directly — purely an internal LLM mechanic you didn't have to touch |
| 11 | Hallucination | Model generating incorrect/fabricated info confidently | **Partially** | Real incidents caught & fixed — e.g., Jira agent inferring the site URL instead of reading config |
| 12 | Vector DB | Database storing embeddings for similarity search | **No** | Named only as a future option (Pinecone/Qdrant/pgvector) in naming conventions — not built |
| 13 | Fine Tuning | Retraining a model on custom data | **No** | Not used anywhere |
| 14 | Prompt Engineering | Crafting instructions to get reliable model behavior | **Yes** | `CLAUDE.md` orchestration instructions, subagent system prompts, Hard Rules |
| 15 | LangChain (Framework) | Framework for chaining LLM calls/agents/tools | **No** | Orchestration is native Claude Code subagents, not LangChain/LangGraph |
| 16 | Claude | Anthropic's model family | **Yes** | Core to everything — Claude Code + Claude.ai |
| 17 | Chunking | Splitting documents into pieces for retrieval | **No** | No retrieval pipeline exists to need this |
| 18 | Knowledge Graph | Structured entity-relationship representation | **Yes** | Not used (Atlassian's own "Teamwork Graph" MCP tools exist but weren't leveraged) |
| 19 | Grounding | Anchoring model output in real source data, not memory | **Partially** | Project docs (`BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) grounded subagent work; business-flows doc grounded the Jira test pack |
| 20 | Multi Agent | Multiple specialized agents collaborating | **Yes** | Master + 4 repo subagents + automation + 2 Jira agents (7 total) |
| 21 | AI Orchestration | Coordinating multiple agents/steps toward a goal | **Yes** | `agent-vkai-master`'s plan → approve → dispatch → log workflow |
| 22 | Plugins | Installable tool/skill bundles extending an agent | **No** | Not used within this project |
| 23 | Caching | Storing results to avoid recomputation/re-fetching | **Partially** | Catalog sync uses a push model with stale-cache pull as fallback — data caching, not AI-specific (e.g. no prompt caching) |
| 24 | Tool Use / Function Calling | Model invoking defined tools (bash, git, APIs) to act, not just talk | **Yes** | Subagents running bash/git/gh commands; Jira MCP tool calls |
| 25 | Human-in-the-Loop | Mandatory human checkpoint before high-risk actions | **Yes** | Every `dev → main` merge, every subagent plan — nothing auto-merges or auto-decides |

heading: Bottom line
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — AI Concepts Inventory (v1) > ## Bottom line
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — AI Concepts Inventory (v1) > ## Bottom line

Strong on the **agentic/orchestration** side: Agentic AI, Multi-Agent, MCP, Context Engineering, Guardrails, Tool Use, Human-in-the-Loop. This is the harder, more interview-impressive half.

Clearest gap: the **RAG/retrieval stack** (Embedding, Vector DB, Chunking, Knowledge Graph, Fine-Tuning, LangChain) exists only as planned folders in `VK-AI-Labs-Naming-Conventions.md`, not as working code. This is the natural next build if you want the full AI-engineer story to hold up end-to-end.

heading: VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys

**Sub-project:** Basic Insurance & Claim Management (Policy, Premium, Claims)
**Companion to:** `vkai-insurance-setup-log.md` (accounts, architecture, DB schema, API contract)
**Status:** Verified against live implementation — full happy-path journey (§5.1) tested end-to-end across both clouds with real data, zero deviations found from this spec
**Last updated:** 2026-08-01

---

heading: 1. Actors
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 1. Actors
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 1. Actors

| Actor | Where they log in | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| **Client (customer)** | Client portal (GCP) | Firebase Auth / Identity Platform |
| **Ops — Reviewer** | Provider portal (Azure) | Entra ID, `VKAI-Insurance-Provider-Reviewers` group |
| **Ops — Approver** | Provider portal (Azure) | Entra ID, `VKAI-Insurance-Provider-Approvers` group |
| **System (background)** | No login — service-to-service | Shared secret (`X-VKAI-Sync-Key`) |

---

### 2. Client-side journeys

heading: 2.1 Registration & login
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.1 Registration & login
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.1 Registration & login

1. New customer lands on `vkai-insurance-client` site, clicks **Sign up**.
2. Firebase Auth handles email/password (or social) signup, issues a JWT session.
3. Client API creates a `users` row (`firebase_uid`, `email`, `name`).
4. Returning customer: **Log in** → Firebase Auth validates → JWT issued → client API validates JWT on every subsequent call.

heading: 2.2 Browse policy catalog
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.2 Browse policy catalog
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.2 Browse policy catalog

1. On login, client app calls client API → client API returns cached `policy_catalog` rows.
2. If `last_synced_at` is stale (e.g., >N minutes old), client API calls provider's `GET /v1/catalog/policies`, refreshes local `policy_catalog` table.
3. Customer sees a list of plans (e.g., "Basic Health Plan") with premium/coverage amounts.

heading: 2.3 Enroll in a policy
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.3 Enroll in a policy
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.3 Enroll in a policy

1. Customer selects a catalog plan → clicks **Enroll**.
2. Client API creates a `policies` row: `status = pending`, `sync_status = pending`.
3. Client API calls `POST /v1/sync/policies` on the provider API (payload includes `event_id`, catalog reference, client user reference).
4. Provider API creates its own `policies` row (`status = pending`, linked to `client_policy_id`), returns success.
5. Client API marks local record `sync_status = synced`.
6. **(Provider-side action, §3.3)** Ops confirms/activates → provider calls `POST /v1/sync/policies/status` back to client → client updates `status = active`.
7. Customer sees policy move from "Pending" to "Active" on their dashboard.

heading: 2.4 Pay premium
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.4 Pay premium
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.4 Pay premium

1. Customer selects an active policy → clicks **Pay premium** (virtual payment — no real gateway).
2. Client API creates a `premiums` row (`amount`, `paid_at`, `sync_status = pending`).
3. Client API calls `POST /v1/sync/premiums` on provider API.
4. Provider API records the payment in its own `premiums` table, confirms.
5. Client marks `sync_status = synced`. Customer sees payment reflected immediately in their history.

heading: 2.5 File a claim
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.5 File a claim
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.5 File a claim

1. Customer opens an active policy → clicks **File a claim** → enters amount + description.
2. Client API creates a `claims` row: `status = Submitted`, `sync_status = pending`.
3. Client API calls `POST /v1/sync/claims` on provider API.
4. Provider API creates its own `claims` row (`status = Submitted`, linked via `client_claim_id`).
5. Client marks `sync_status = synced`. Customer sees the claim listed under the policy with status "Submitted."

heading: 2.6 Track claim status
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.6 Track claim status
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.6 Track claim status

1. Customer revisits the policy page any time → sees current claim status, pulled from the client's own `claims` table (always up to date because provider pushes status changes — see §3.5–3.7).
2. No polling needed on the client side; status updates arrive via `POST /v1/sync/claims/status` whenever ops changes something.

heading: 2.7 Renew policy
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.7 Renew policy
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.7 Renew policy

1. Client app flags policies where `expiry_date` is within a configurable window (e.g., 30 days).
2. Customer clicks **Renew** → same flow as 2.3 (new enrollment cycle), or — simpler for a demo — client API extends `expiry_date` on the existing `policies` row and syncs the renewal as an update via `POST /v1/sync/policies` with `event_type: policy.renewed`.
3. Provider updates its mirrored record; may or may not require Approver sign-off (kept as a client-driven self-service action for simplicity, since it's a renewal of an already-approved policy, not a new one).

heading: 2.8 Consolidated policy view (dashboard)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.8 Consolidated policy view (dashboard)
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 2. Client-side journeys > ### 2.8 Consolidated policy view (dashboard)

1. Customer's home page after login shows: list of policies, each with nested premium payment history and claim history — everything grouped under the policy record, per your original requirement #4.
2. All of this is a single client API call (`GET /v1/policies?include=premiums,claims`) reading from the client's own DB — no live cross-cloud call needed for display, since sync already wrote everything locally.

---

### 3. Provider-side journeys

heading: 3.1 Ops login
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.1 Ops login
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.1 Ops login

1. Ops person navigates to `vkai-insurance-provider` portal.
2. Redirected to Entra ID login (their individual account).
3. On successful auth, Entra ID token includes group membership → provider API maps this to `Reviewer` or `Approver` role, creates/updates the `ops_users` row (`entra_object_id`, `email`, `role`).
4. Portal UI adapts: Reviewers see review actions only; Approvers see full action set.

heading: 3.2 Manage policy catalog
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.2 Manage policy catalog
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.2 Manage policy catalog

1. An Approver (catalog changes are a higher-trust action) creates/edits/deactivates a plan in `policy_catalog` (name, premium, coverage, active flag).
2. This is provider-side only — no sync needed outbound, since client pulls the catalog on its own schedule (§2.2).

heading: 3.3 Review new enrollment & activate policy
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.3 Review new enrollment & activate policy
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.3 Review new enrollment & activate policy

1. New enrollment arrives via `POST /v1/sync/policies` (from §2.3) → lands in provider's `policies` table, `status = pending`.
2. Ops (Reviewer or Approver) sees it in a "Pending enrollments" queue, reviews basic details.
3. Approver clicks **Activate** → `status = active` in provider DB.
4. Provider API calls `POST /v1/sync/policies/status` → client updates its own record to `active`.

heading: 3.4 Process premium payment
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.4 Process premium payment
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.4 Process premium payment

1. Premium payment arrives via `POST /v1/sync/premiums` (from §2.4) → recorded directly in provider's `premiums` table.
2. Since payments are virtual/no gateway, this is largely a passive "received and recorded" event — ops can view payment history per policy but no approval action is required here for the basic scope.

heading: 3.5 Review claim (Reviewer)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.5 Review claim (Reviewer)
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.5 Review claim (Reviewer)

1. New claim arrives via `POST /v1/sync/claims` → provider `claims` table, `status = Submitted`.
2. Reviewer opens the claim, checks details, clicks **Move to Under Review** → `status = Under Review`, `reviewed_by = <ops_user_id>`.
3. Provider API calls `POST /v1/sync/claims/status` → client updates to "Under Review."

heading: 3.6 Approve or reject claim (Approver)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.6 Approve or reject claim (Approver)
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.6 Approve or reject claim (Approver)

1. Approver opens a claim in "Under Review" → decides **Approve** or **Reject**.
2. `status = Approved` or `Rejected`, `approved_by = <ops_user_id>`.
3. Provider API calls `POST /v1/sync/claims/status` → client reflects the decision.

heading: 3.7 Mark claim as paid
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.7 Mark claim as paid
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.7 Mark claim as paid

1. For an `Approved` claim, Approver clicks **Mark as Paid** (virtual payout — figure recorded, no real transfer).
2. `status = Paid`.
3. Provider API calls `POST /v1/sync/claims/status` → client shows final "Paid" status.

heading: 3.8 Sync issues view
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.8 Sync issues view
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 3. Provider-side journeys > ### 3.8 Sync issues view

1. Ops (either role) can open a **"Sync issues"** screen listing any local records (`policies`/`premiums`/`claims`) where `sync_status = failed` after the retry job has exhausted its capped attempts.
2. Each row shows the record type, business ID, last attempt time, and attempt count — enough to spot a stuck cross-cloud sync without digging through logs.
3. No manual "force retry" button needed for the basic scope — this is a visibility screen, not an admin tool; the background job keeps retrying on its own schedule regardless.
4. Same pattern exists on the client side too, if you want customers' failed syncs visible to them — recommend keeping that client-side one **internal/admin-only** for now rather than customer-facing, since a customer seeing "sync failed" without context is more confusing than reassuring. Can revisit later.

---

heading: 4. Cross-cloud sync flows (system-level, background)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 4. Cross-cloud sync flows (system-level, background)
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 4. Cross-cloud sync flows (system-level, background)

These run automatically as a side effect of the actions above — no user directly triggers them, but they're worth documenting as their own flows since they're the backbone of the "fully independent, no shared DB" design.

| # | Flow | Trigger | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Catalog sync | Client portal load / cache expiry | Provider → Client (pulled) |
| 4.2 | Enrollment sync | Customer enrolls | Client → Provider (pushed) |
| 4.3 | Enrollment status sync | Ops activates policy | Provider → Client (pushed) |
| 4.4 | Premium sync | Customer pays premium | Client → Provider (pushed) |
| 4.5 | Claim submission sync | Customer files claim | Client → Provider (pushed) |
| 4.6 | Claim status sync | Ops changes claim status (any transition) | Provider → Client (pushed) |
| 4.7 | Retry sync | Any of the above fails (`sync_status = failed`) | Background job, same side that originated the call |

**Retry flow (4.7) in detail:**
1. Outbound sync call fails (timeout, other side down, etc.) → record stays `sync_status = failed`.
2. Background job (`node-cron`, runs every few minutes) queries local table for `sync_status IN ('pending', 'failed')`.
3. Retries the call with the same `event_id` (idempotency-safe on the receiving end).
4. On success → `sync_status = synced`. After a capped number of attempts, stays `failed` and is surfaced in the "Sync issues" view (§3.8) for ops/admin visibility (no paging/alerting needed for a demo).

**Confirmed via live testing (2026-08-01):** this retry mechanism works exactly as designed — a genuinely failed enrollment sync (from an early integration bug, since fixed) was automatically picked up and successfully retried by the background job with no manual intervention, once the underlying code issue was corrected. All 6 sync endpoints in §4's table have now been exercised live end-to-end with real data across both clouds, with zero deviation from the flows described in this document.

### 5. End-to-end journey narratives

heading: 5.1 Happy path — enroll, pay, claim, get paid
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 5. End-to-end journey narratives > ### 5.1 Happy path — enroll, pay, claim, get paid
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 5. End-to-end journey narratives > ### 5.1 Happy path — enroll, pay, claim, get paid

1. Customer signs up → browses catalog → enrolls in "Basic Health Plan" (§2.1–2.3)
2. Provider Approver activates the policy (§3.3) → customer sees "Active"
3. Customer pays premium (§2.4) → provider records it (§3.4)
4. Later, customer files a claim for $500 (§2.5)
5. Provider Reviewer moves it to "Under Review" (§3.5) → customer sees status update in real time
6. Provider Approver approves it, then marks it "Paid" (§3.6–3.7)
7. Customer's dashboard shows the full history: policy → premium paid → claim → Paid, all under one login (§2.8)

heading: 5.2 Renewal near expiry
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 5. End-to-end journey narratives > ### 5.2 Renewal near expiry
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 5. End-to-end journey narratives > ### 5.2 Renewal near expiry

1. Customer's policy shows `expiry_date` within 30 days → "Renew" prompt appears (§2.7)
2. Customer renews → client extends `expiry_date`, syncs the update to provider
3. Provider mirrors the new expiry date — no re-approval needed since it's an existing, already-active policy

heading: 5.3 Claim rejected
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 5. End-to-end journey narratives > ### 5.3 Claim rejected
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 5. End-to-end journey narratives > ### 5.3 Claim rejected

1. Customer files a claim (§2.5) → Reviewer reviews it (§3.5)
2. Approver rejects it, citing it falls outside coverage terms (§3.6, `status = Rejected`)
3. Customer sees "Rejected" on their dashboard — no payment record created, claim journey ends here

heading: 6. Edge cases & exception flows
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 6. Edge cases & exception flows
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 6. Edge cases & exception flows

| Scenario | Handling |
|---|---|
| Cross-cloud sync call fails (network blip, other cloud down) | `sync_status = failed`, retried automatically (§4.7); user isn't blocked — their local record still shows correctly on their own side, just flagged internally as not-yet-synced |
| Duplicate sync delivery (retry after a slow-but-successful original call) | Receiving side checks `event_id` — already-processed events are no-ops, preventing double records |
| Customer tries to file a claim on an expired/pending (not yet active) policy | Client API blocks the action client-side — claims only allowed on `status = active` policies |
| Ops tries to approve a claim that's still "Submitted" (skipped review) | Basic scope allows Approver to act on any status for flexibility (single generic ops workflow, no strict gating) — can be tightened later if you want to enforce Reviewer-first |
| Policy catalog changes after a customer already enrolled | Existing enrollments are unaffected — `policies` rows carry a snapshot reference at enrollment time (`policy_catalog_id`), catalog edits only affect future enrollments |

---

breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 7. Decisions confirmed on this document
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Platform: Business Flows & User Journeys > ## 7. Decisions confirmed on this document

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Renewal is self-service** — no ops approval step; client extends `expiry_date` and syncs the update directly (§2.7, §5.2). |
| 2 | **Claim workflow order is flexible** — an Approver can act on a claim regardless of whether a Reviewer touched it first; not strictly gated (§3.6). |
| 3 | **Sync issues view added** — ops can see permanently-failed cross-cloud syncs after retries are exhausted (§3.8). |

heading: 4. Credential & config strategy
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 4. Credential & config strategy
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 4. Credential & config strategy

**Env-var-first, gitignored-local-file fallback** — identical key names work in both local and CI:

1. `ConfigReader` checks `System.getenv()` first
2. Falls back to `config-local.properties` (gitignored; never committed)
3. `config-local.properties.example` (placeholder keys only) is the committed template
4. In CI, the same key names are **GitHub Actions repository secrets** (`VKAI_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `VKAI_CLIENT_PASSWORD`), injected as env vars

**QA account:** a dedicated Firebase account on the client portal (`vkailabs@gmail.com`), created manually, kept separate from personal identities. **No provider/Entra QA credentials are used by this framework** — see §5.

**Dynamic emails:** `TestData.uniqueClientEmail()` generates Gmail plus-addressed variants (`vkailabs+<tag>@gmail.com`) for non-idempotent flows like registration. A safety guard normalizes and validates every signup submission against the configured QA email pattern before submitting — this exists because a real personal email was accidentally used once during manual DOM-capture work; the guard makes that fail loudly instead of silently creating a stray account.

**Accepted test-data pollution:** every enrollment run creates a real pending policy on the live client dev DB; every registration run creates a real Firebase account (plus-addressed). Both are accepted trade-offs (documented in `docs/TRIAGE.md`) — this is a dedicated QA-only account, so pollution has no real-world cost. No cleanup automation exists or is planned.

heading: 5. The architectural constraint: why there's no provider-side UI automation
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 5. The architectural constraint: why there's no provider-side UI automation
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 5. The architectural constraint: why there's no provider-side UI automation

This is the single most important thing to understand before extending this framework. Full investigation is in setup log §25.3 — summarized here:

- **Microsoft Entra ID Security Defaults is enabled tenant-wide**, and the dedicated Approver QA account has **no MFA method registered** — meaning any login attempt (automated or manual) risks triggering forced MFA enrollment, which Selenium cannot complete.
- This also **rules out MSAL ROPC token-bypass** — Microsoft blocks ROPC when Security Defaults/Conditional Access MFA is enforced.
- Direct (read-only) investigation of `vkai-insurance-provider-api`'s route code confirmed the Approver-action endpoints (`activate`, `approve`, `reject`, `mark-paid`) are **exclusively Entra-JWT-gated**, with no service-account or API-key path.
- A fixture-seam design (env-gated, non-prod-only test endpoints) was **specified but never built** — see §8, this path was deliberately closed.
- Using a personal/admin Entra account instead of a QA account **was considered and rejected** — Security Defaults is tenant-wide, not account-specific, so it wouldn't have bypassed anything, and it would have introduced real credential-exposure risk for no benefit.

**Practical consequence:** any scenario requiring a provider login or a provider action is out of scope for this framework, permanently, absent a future deliberate decision to reopen this (see §9).

---

heading: 6. Live-DOM discipline — the pattern behind every build cycle
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 6. Live-DOM discipline — the pattern behind every build cycle
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 6. Live-DOM discipline — the pattern behind every build cycle

Every locator in this framework was built from **real, observed DOM**, never guessed from the business-flows spec alone. This is a deliberate practice, not incidental:

- DOM captures came from the browser console (`copy(document.querySelector('#root').innerHTML)` or a summarized headings/buttons/testids JSON), taken live by a human, then handed to the builder
- This caught real issues that guessing would have missed: a DOM capture once came from the wrong portal (provider instead of client) and was caught before any code was built against it; a status locator based on literal text (`"Pending"`) failed on its first live run because the actual rendered text was lowercase (`"pending"`) — fixed by locating on CSS class instead of text
- **The app has no `data-testid` attributes anywhere** — every locator leans on structural/class-based selectors or exact text matching. This makes the suite more fragile to UI changes than a test-id-based suite would be; adding `data-testid`s to the client app is a flagged-but-not-actioned improvement (would require changes in `vkai-insurance-client`, out of this repo's scope)

**If extending this framework:** don't write a locator against assumed markup. Get a live capture first, every time.

That heading is **unchanged and still present** in VKAI-006 (verified against committed client code `bce5c29` — `

Your policies

`, with the two new `.policy-section` blocks added *below* it), but the loaded marker was nonetheless re-grounded onto the confirmed-unchanged, unambiguous `div.policy-summary` block as a more durable dashboard-content marker. `DASH-001`'s positional assertion **keeps its original "Your policies" target** (the heading persists), preserving its VKAI-005 intent. - **DASH-004 (no Jira issue — deliberate)** — the empty-section boundary: an empty bucket still renders its section, showing `

` with exact text "No active policies." / "No pending policies." (trailing period) instead of a card grid. Same disposition as DASH-002 — **not** currently reproducible UI-only (QA account Active=5/Pending=54, neither empty; activation provider-side, client UI can't delete policies), held `@Manual`, deliberately **no** Jira issue, a data-state limitation and **not** one of the deleted 30. (Distinct precedence: when total policies == 0, neither section renders — the pre-existing `.empty-state` "No policies yet" block shows instead.) Needs a reproducible empty-bucket state + a fresh live DOM capture before automating. Do not fake an empty state. **Wording mismatches found and reconciled** (spec said one thing, app says another — always trust the live app, update the spec): - VJS-3: pack said "Email already in use" → real text "An account with that email already exists." - VJS-4: `user@domain` removed from the outline — HTML5 validation accepts it as valid (no TLD required), contradicting the pack's assumption it'd be rejected - VJS-6: pack said "Invalid credentials" → real text "Incorrect email or password." ---

heading: 8. Scope: the architectural boundary is closed, the scenario count is not (2026-08-14)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 8. Scope: the architectural boundary is closed, the scenario count is not (2026-08-14)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 8. Scope: the architectural boundary is closed, the scenario count is not (2026-08-14)

**Read this carefully — this section's title used to say "closed at 10," which is now misleading.** What's permanently closed is the *boundary*: UI-automation only, no API-level test automation, no manual/exploratory scenario tracking, no provider/Entra actions. The *scenario count inside that boundary* is expected to grow over time as new stories ship genuinely-new client UI — the 3 added for `VKAI-005` and the 1 automated for `VKAI-006` (DASH-003) bring the live total to 13 automated (from the original 10), plus 2 held `@Manual` (DASH-002, DASH-004). Don't be confused if a future count is higher than what's written here; check §7 for the current live table.

The original regression pack had 40 scenarios. **30 were evaluated, found to require either provider/Entra actions (§5) or backend-only behavior with no UI surface, and were permanently deleted from Jira** — not deferred, not labeled-and-kept, actually removed. This followed an explicit instruction to lock scope at **UI-automation only — no API-level test automation, no manual/exploratory scenario tracking**.

Two paths that could have closed the gap were considered and explicitly declined:
- **The fixture-seam approach** (`docs/provider-fixture-endpoints-spec.md`, marked OBSOLETE/CLOSED) — would have let tests call provider endpoints directly with a scoped test credential. Rejected as it constitutes API-level automation.
- **Manual/exploratory tracking** of provider actions — rejected as it constitutes manual scenario execution.

A specific request to cover the full provider-inclusive E2E lifecycle (create → enroll → activate → pay → claim → review → approve → paid, with status checks throughout) was evaluated and declined on the same grounds.

`docs/TRIAGE.md` in the repo is the closed-scope record (not a roadmap) — it documents what was cut and why, for anyone who later wonders "why isn't X automated."

heading: 9. If you're extending this framework
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 9. If you're extending this framework
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Automation Reference v1 > ## 9. If you're extending this framework

**Read this before adding scenario #11.**

- **Genuinely new UI-only territory** (a client-side flow that was never in the original 40, or a variant nobody's tested yet) — fair game, follow the same loop: propose the Gherkin, add it to the regression pack file, get a live DOM capture, build, verify, commit via the usual `dev → main` PR flow.
- **Anything from the deleted 30** (provider actions, active-policy-dependent happy paths, backend-only sync behavior) — **this is not a "just add it" request.** It requires consciously reopening the scope-lock decision in §8, with the same explicit trade-off discussion as before (does this mean building the fixture seam? does this mean tracking manual tests? is that actually what's wanted, or is there a new idea for solving §5's MFA blocker?). Don't quietly build toward this without that conversation happening first.
- **Git workflow:** `dev` for work, PR to protected `main`, same as the other 4 repos. Expect to see "X commits ahead/behind" messages between merges — this is normal merge-commit bookkeeping, not drift; don't chase it to zero. Global git identity is `vkailabs`; this repo also has it set per-repo explicitly.
- **Credentials:** never paste real values into a chat session, ever, even QA-only ones. Use the local `config-local.properties` file directly.

heading: Scope Change (2026-08-14)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Test Pack v1 > ## Scope Change (2026-08-14)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Regression Test Pack v1 > ## Scope Change (2026-08-14)

This pack originally covered all 40 regression scenarios across the full system (client, provider, cross-cloud sync). Following the build of the automation framework and discovery of a real architectural blocker — Microsoft Entra ID Security Defaults + no MFA-exempt account rules out UI-automating provider Approver logins, and the API endpoints for those actions are Entra-JWT-gated with no service-account path — a decision was made to **scope this regression pack down to UI-automatable scenarios only**:

- No API-level test automation
- No manual/exploratory scenarios tracked in this pack (provider Approver actions, backend-only sync behavior)
- Pure browser/UI automation only, client-side (Firebase Auth), via Selenium/Cucumber/TestNG

**30 scenarios were removed** from this pack and correspondingly deleted from Jira (2026-08-14, after a brief interim period as `descoped`-labeled issues), locking the pack to **UI-automation only** — client-side, no provider/Entra actions, no API, no manual tracking. That boundary is what's fixed, not a frozen scenario count: new genuinely-UI-only scenarios (like the 3 added below for `VKAI-005`) are expected to be added over time as stories ship, as long as they stay within this boundary. See the setup log for the full architectural rationale (the Entra ID MFA blocker) behind the original scope-down.

# VK AI Labs — Insurance Ecosystem: Setup & Progress Log > ## 2. Project Scope Recap

- **Client side:** website where a customer buys a medical insurance policy, pays premium, and files/tracks claims.
- **Provider side:** website where the service provider processes policy applications, premiums, and claims.
- Claim/policy/premium details created on the provider side must surface back to the client under their login (grouped under the policy record).
- Client and provider are **fully independent** — separate codebases, separate deploy lifecycles, separate APIs, separate databases.
- Stack: React (frontend, on Vercel) + Node.js (API, on cloud VMs) + Azure & GCP (dual-cloud, cloud-split by side) + GitHub (source + CI/CD) + VS Code (local dev).

heading: 8. Decisions Log
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Ecosystem: Setup & Progress Log > ## 8. Decisions Log
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Ecosystem: Setup & Progress Log > ## 8. Decisions Log

*(D1–D30 unchanged from Phase 3 — see prior log versions or the "what/why recap" doc for the full list: repo/branch structure, dual-cloud split, no shared DB, native auth per cloud, Entra ID token fixes, Docker networking fixes, sync bug fixes, etc.)*

| ID | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| D31 | GitHub branch protection's "Required approvals" set to 0 on all 4 repos | Solo account can't approve its own PR — GitHub blocks this even for repo owners/admins |
| D32 | All 4 repos' `dev` merged into `main` before any deployment | Establishes `main` as "what's actually running in production" from Phase 4 onward |
| D33 | Both frontends deploy to Vercel (not Azure App Service for the provider portal) | Matches the original Phase 1 plan; keeps both frontends on one free, consistent, zero-maintenance platform |
| D34 | Provider API's VM ended up in `centralus` with size `Standard_D2ads_v6`, in a resource group `rg-vkai-insurance-dev` (not the originally-planned `eastus`/free-tier B-series) | Region/SKU availability constraints during setup meant the originally planned `eastus` + `B1s`/`B2s` combination could not be provisioned; `centralus` with a different VM size was the path that worked. Cost is modest (~$22.66/month) and covered by remaining Azure credit for now; documented as a deviation from the original free-tier-only plan (see §14 for the full troubleshooting path) |
| D35 | SSL for both API VMs uses `nip.io` (free wildcard DNS resolving an IP to a usable hostname) rather than a purchased domain | Consistent with the Phase 4 planning decision to skip buying a custom domain; Let's Encrypt just needs a resolvable hostname, which `nip.io` provides for free |
| D36 | Vercel projects use a `vercel.json` rewrite rule (`{"rewrites": [{"source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html"}]}`) | React Router SPAs need this so direct navigation/refresh on any non-root route (e.g. `/login`) doesn't 404 — only `index.html` exists as a real static file on Vercel; all other routes only exist client-side after the JS loads |
| D37 | MSAL's `redirectUri`/`postLogoutRedirectUri` use `window.location.origin` instead of a hardcoded URL | The original code hardcoded `http://localhost:5174`, which broke login entirely once deployed to a different domain (Vercel) — using `window.location.origin` makes it correct automatically in any environment without per-environment config |
| D38 | All infrastructure/config fixes must be committed through the repo (local `dev` branch → PR → `main` → pull on the VM), never left as a standalone manual edit on a VM's disk | A CORS fix made directly on the VM via `nano` was never committed, so it silently "disappeared" from the deployment the next time the VM's containers were recreated — the VM's disk is not a source of truth, only the repo is |
| D39 | Client frontend (`vkai-insurance-client`) got the same `vercel.json` SPA rewrite rule already applied to the provider frontend | Same root cause as D36 — only `index.html` exists as a real static file on Vercel, so direct navigation/refresh on non-root routes 404s without this rule |
| D40 | The solution architecture diagram (`vkai-insurance-solution-architecture-v2.drawio`) is treated as a **living file**, iterated directly in draw.io (both via Claude's draw.io connector and the owner's own manual edits in the app), rather than a one-time export | The diagram needed several rounds of correction (real stencils, connector routing, label styling — see §22) as it was actively worked on; keeping it editable in its native format, with the `.html`/PNG exports regenerated from it on request, avoids the exports silently drifting out of sync with the source |

heading: 14.1 VM creation — a longer path than expected
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs — Insurance Ecosystem: Setup & Progress Log > ## 14. Phase 4 — Azure Provider API: Live Deployment > ### 14.1 VM creation — a longer path than expected
text:
# VK AI Labs — Insurance Ecosystem: Setup & Progress Log > ## 14. Phase 4 — Azure Provider API: Live Deployment > ### 14.1 VM creation — a longer path than expected

The original plan (mirroring the GCP approach exactly) was: `Standard_B1s` in `eastus`, matching Azure's free-tier VM allowance. This did not work as planned — multiple region and size combinations (`eastus`/`B1s`, `eastus2`/`B1s`, `centralus`/`B1s`, `eastus`/`B2ats_v2`, `eastus`/`B2s`, `westus2`/`B2s`) all failed with capacity/availability errors.

**Troubleshooting path that resolved it:**
1. Confirmed `Microsoft.Compute`, `Microsoft.Network`, and `Microsoft.Storage` resource providers were registered on the subscription (they initially were not — registering them was a necessary but not sufficient fix).
2. Used the Azure Portal's built-in quota troubleshooter (via **Usage + quotas**), which identified the subscription was still effectively on a restricted quota tier despite showing nominal limits.
3. Upgraded the subscription's billing plan from Free Trial to **Azure Plan** (Pay-As-You-Go) — existing $200-equivalent credit carried over fully, no separate charge for the upgrade itself.
4. Even after the upgrade, `eastus`/`eastus2` continued showing capacity restrictions for small B-series sizes specifically.
5. Ultimately succeeded via the **Azure Portal UI** (not CLI) in the **`centralus`** region, **Zone 1**, using **`Standard_D2ads_v6`** — a larger, non-free-tier size, at approximately **$22.66/month**.
6. An earlier accidental deployment (via the Portal wizard defaulting to `Standard_D2ads_v6` in a different zone before the final successful one) was found, fully deleted (VM, disk, NIC, and public IP all individually confirmed removed) to avoid orphaned billable resources, before the final correct deployment.

**Resulting resource group:** `rg-vkai-insurance-dev` (created directly via Portal at this point in the process, hence the naming deviation noted in §3) — contains the VM, its NSG, VNet, and static Standard-SKU public IP (`20.80.90.33`).

### 15. Phase 4 — Both Frontends: Live Deployment to Vercel

heading: 15.1 Client frontend
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 15. Phase 4 — Both Frontends: Live Deployment to Vercel > ### 15.1 Client frontend
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 15. Phase 4 — Both Frontends: Live Deployment to Vercel > ### 15.1 Client frontend

Deployed from `main` via Vercel's existing GitHub integration (project was linked back in Phase 1). Production environment variables configured in the Vercel dashboard (Firebase config values, `VITE_VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL` pointing to the live GCP API). Deployed successfully to `https://vkai-insurance-client.vercel.app`.

**Bug found and fixed during this step:** the client API's `docker-compose.yml` explicitly lists which environment variables get passed into the container, rather than loading the whole `.env` file — and `VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (needed for CORS once a real frontend domain existed) had never been added to that list, even though it existed correctly in `.env` itself and in the application code. The variable was silently missing from the running container, causing CORS to keep rejecting the Vercel origin even after `.env` was correctly updated and the container rebuilt. **Fixed** by adding the missing line to `docker-compose.yml` and forcing a full `docker compose down` + `up` (a `--build` alone was not sufficient to pick up the compose file change).

heading: 15.2 Provider frontend
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 15. Phase 4 — Both Frontends: Live Deployment to Vercel > ### 15.2 Provider frontend
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 15. Phase 4 — Both Frontends: Live Deployment to Vercel > ### 15.2 Provider frontend

This project had **already auto-deployed** from `main` via Vercel's default behavior (deploy-on-push), before its environment variables were ever manually configured — discovered when its `/login` page loaded but Microsoft sign-in failed with `AADSTS900023: Specified tenant identifier 'undefined'`, confirming the Entra ID env vars were entirely unset in Vercel.

**Steps taken to fully wire it up:**
1. Added `https://vkai-insurance-provider.vercel.app` as an authorized redirect URI in the Entra ID app registration (alongside the existing `http://localhost:5174`).
2. Added all 5 required environment variables (API base URL + 4 Entra ID values) in Vercel's dashboard for the Production environment.
3. Updated the provider API's `VKAI_INSURANCE_PROVIDER_API_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` to the new Vercel origin and did a full `docker compose down` + `up` (this repo's `docker-compose.yml` already correctly included this variable in its explicit list, unlike the client API — no additional fix needed here).
4. Redeployed the frontend from Vercel's dashboard to pick up the new env vars (env var changes don't apply retroactively to already-built deployments).

**Two further bugs found and fixed after this:**
- **SPA routing 404:** direct navigation to `/login` returned a Vercel 404, since only `index.html` exists as a real static file and all other routes only exist client-side via React Router. **Fixed** by adding a `vercel.json` rewrite rule so any non-asset path serves `index.html` (see D36).
- **Hardcoded MSAL redirect URI:** `src/authConfig.js` had `redirectUri` and `postLogoutRedirectUri` both hardcoded to `http://localhost:5174`, so login attempted to redirect back to `localhost` even when running on the live Vercel domain, causing `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`. **Fixed** by switching both to `window.location.origin`, which resolves correctly in any environment automatically (see D37).

**Result:** Entra ID login on the deployed provider portal now works end-to-end. A first production policy catalog entry ("Basic Health Plan," $100 premium, $5000 coverage) was created and confirmed displaying correctly.

heading: 16. Known Issues / Gotchas — Phase 4 (continued)
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 16. Known Issues / Gotchas — Phase 4 (continued)
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 16. Known Issues / Gotchas — Phase 4 (continued)

*(§14 entries from the earlier log version — solo-account PR self-approval, a hung PR-creation UI, checking `docker --version` from the wrong shell after `exit`, port 4000 correctly staying closed, `nslookup` not installed by default — still apply, see prior version.)*

- **Azure region/SKU capacity issues took significant troubleshooting** to resolve — see the full path in §14.1. The eventual working combination (`centralus`, `Standard_D2ads_v6`) differs from the originally planned free-tier target (`eastus`, `Standard_B1s`), representing a real, if modest, ongoing cost (~$22.66/month) rather than the originally intended $0.
- **Azure's auto-generated NSG name** (`vm-vkai-insurance-provider-api-devNSG`) doesn't follow this project's kebab-case convention (no hyphen before "NSG") — this is Azure's own default naming behavior when a resource group is created via the Portal wizard's automatic resource naming, not something explicitly configured. Noted, not corrected, since renaming would require recreating the NSG.
- **A `docker-compose.yml`'s explicit environment-variable list can silently omit a variable** that exists correctly in both `.env` and the application code — the app just receives `undefined` for it with no error, which can look identical to a CORS misconfiguration until checked directly with `docker compose exec api env | grep <VAR>`. Worth checking this specifically (compare the compose file's `environment:` list against `.env.example`) whenever adding a new env var to an already-built repo's deployment config.
- **`docker compose up --build -d` alone does not guarant­ee an existing container picks up a `docker-compose.yml` change** — `docker compose down` followed by `up -d` forces a full, clean recreate and reliably picks up any compose-file-level changes (like a newly added environment variable), where `--build` alone may not.
- **React Router SPAs deployed to Vercel need an explicit rewrite rule** (`vercel.json`) or direct navigation/refresh on any non-root route 404s — this is a standard, well-known SPA-hosting requirement, not specific to this project, but easy to miss until actually testing a direct URL rather than only ever navigating via in-app links.
- **Hardcoded environment-specific values (like a redirect URI) will silently break the moment code runs anywhere other than where it was originally tested** — `window.location.origin` (or equivalent dynamic resolution) is the correct pattern for anything that needs to "know its own URL," rather than a fixed string.

The `vkailabs@gmail.com` account (owning the GCP project and Firebase project) was temporarily inaccessible for a few days, during which the client API's VM was stopped by GCP (`TERMINATED` state). Once account access was restored:

- VM restarted cleanly via `gcloud compute instances start` — no data loss, static IP unchanged (`146.148.64.235`), Postgres volume intact.
- Docker containers required a manual `docker compose up -d` on reconnect (no `systemd`-level auto-start was configured for the compose stack itself, only the containers' own `restart: unless-stopped` policy, which only helps if the *engine* is already running — worth knowing if the VM is ever stopped/started again).
- SSL certificate was still valid throughout (issued 2026-08-01, expires 2026-10-30) — no renewal issues from the downtime window.

heading: 17.2 CORS gap resurfaced — root cause was a deeper process gap, not a fresh bug
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 17. Phase 4 — Recovery, Client SPA Fix & Full Production E2E Verification (2026-08-02) > ### 17.2 CORS gap resurfaced — root cause was a deeper process gap, not a fresh bug
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 17. Phase 4 — Recovery, Client SPA Fix & Full Production E2E Verification (2026-08-02) > ### 17.2 CORS gap resurfaced — root cause was a deeper process gap, not a fresh bug

After bringing the VM back up, CORS broke again (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` reverting to `http://localhost:5173`). Investigation revealed the **real** root cause: the original fix for this (documented in §15.1) had been made by editing `docker-compose.yml` **directly on the VM via `nano`**, and was never actually committed back to the GitHub repo. It wasn't lost by the restart — it simply never existed in git in the first place, so the `main` branch (and thus anything cloned/pulled from it) never had the fix.

**Corrected properly this time:** the fix was made through the normal workflow — local `dev` branch → Claude Code → commit → push → PR → merge to `main` → `git pull origin main` on the VM → `docker compose down && up --build -d`. This ensures the fix is now durable and will survive any future VM recreation or fresh clone.

**New standing lesson (see D38):** any manual edit made directly on a VM (via `nano`, `vim`, etc.) is **local-only** and invisible to git unless explicitly committed and pushed — it should be treated as a temporary/emergency patch at best, never a permanent fix, since the VM's disk is not a source of truth the way the repo is.
