# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 18. Phase 5 — Mobile Responsiveness, Full Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (2026-08-03) > ### 18.1 Mobile responsive fixes, both frontends

Both frontends had nav bar layout bugs on mobile Safari, found via real device testing (not caught by desktop testing alone):

- **Provider frontend** (`vkai-insurance-provider`) — the nav's link list didn't collapse on small screens, overlapping page content. Fixed with a standard responsive pattern: a hamburger toggle below 768px, expanding a dropdown menu (links + user info + Logout); desktop layout (≥768px) left byte-for-byte unchanged. Verified via a temporary static harness mirroring the real component markup/CSS (since NavBar only renders behind a live Entra ID login), then confirmed on both a real mobile Safari session and desktop Chrome.
- **Client frontend** (`vkai-insurance-client`) — same category of bug, but a lighter fix was chosen deliberately: this nav only has brand + 2 links + username + Logout, so a full hamburger menu was judged overkill. Fixed instead with a CSS-only responsive stacking layout (nav becomes two full-width rows below 768px, username truncates with ellipsis, Logout button stays fixed-width and always visible). Same verification approach (temporary harness, confirmed live on both platforms).

**Lesson reinforced:** matching the fix's complexity to the actual UI's complexity (hamburger for a multi-page nav, simple stacking for a minimal one) rather than copy-pasting the same pattern everywhere.

heading: 18.3 Multi-agent orchestration system — design & build
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 18. Phase 5 — Mobile Responsiveness, Full Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (2026-08-03) > ### 18.3 Multi-agent orchestration system — design & build
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 18. Phase 5 — Mobile Responsiveness, Full Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (2026-08-03) > ### 18.3 Multi-agent orchestration system — design & build

A master/subagent system was designed and built on top of Claude Code's native subagent feature (markdown files with YAML frontmatter in `.claude/agents/`, invoked by a parent/orchestrating session), living at the parent folder level (`~/vkai-labs/insurance/`, one level above all 4 repos).

**Structure:**

```
~/vkai-labs/insurance/
├── CLAUDE.md                          ← orchestration instructions for "agent-vkai-master"
├── Story.md                           ← append-only story log, VKAI-XXX numbered
├── .claude/agents/
│   ├── subAgent-vkai-client.md
│   ├── subAgent-vkai-client-api.md
│   ├── subAgent-vkai-provider.md
│   └── subAgent-vkai-provider-api.md
├── vkai-insurance-client/             (existing repo)
├── vkai-insurance-client-api/         (existing repo)
├── vkai-insurance-provider/           (existing repo)
└── vkai-insurance-provider-api/       (existing repo)
```

**How it works:**
- Opening a Claude Code session at the parent folder (not inside any single repo) makes it read the top-level `CLAUDE.md` and become the orchestrator, referred to as `agent-vkai-master`.
- Given a Story (plain-language requirement, optionally with a human-assigned `VKAI-XXX` number — honored as-given if provided, otherwise auto-assigned as the next sequential number based on `Story.md`), the master reads the relevant repos' `BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, determines which subagent(s) are needed and in what dependency-aware order, and **asks clarifying questions on any ambiguity rather than guessing.**
- The master presents a plan and **waits for explicit human approval** before invoking anything.
- Each subagent is scoped to exactly one repo (enforced by convention/instruction, not technical sandboxing — same trust model used throughout this project), reads that repo's own docs first, does the work, commits and pushes to that repo's `dev` branch only, and **never opens or merges a PR** — that remains a manual human step for every story, matching the existing git discipline used everywhere else in this project.
- The master logs the outcome to `Story.md` and reminds the human which PRs still need manual merging.

**Important technical/process notes:**
- Subagent isolation is convention-based, not a hard technical wall — each subagent's system prompt explicitly instructs it to touch only its own repo folder and flag (not act on) anything that seems to require a sibling repo's changes.
- Subagents start with a fresh context window per invocation — the master must pass all necessary context explicitly in each invocation prompt, since subagents can't see the master's own conversation history.
- A standing rule was added to all 4 subagent definitions after the first real story exposed a gap: **if a change is significant (new field, new business rule, new gotcha), update the repo's own `BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` as part of the same commit** — this wasn't in the original subagent instructions and had to be retrofitted (see §18.4).

heading: 18.4 First real story — VKAI-001 (originally requested as VKAI-101)
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 18. Phase 5 — Mobile Responsiveness, Full Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (2026-08-03) > ### 18.4 First real story — VKAI-001 (originally requested as VKAI-101)
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 18. Phase 5 — Mobile Responsiveness, Full Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (2026-08-03) > ### 18.4 First real story — VKAI-001 (originally requested as VKAI-101)

A genuinely non-trivial story was used as the first live test: adding an auto-generated, locked "key" field to policy catalog entries (derived from initials of the name, with collision handling), displayed as a prefix wherever the catalog appears.

**Numbering note:** the story was submitted with an explicit `VKAI-101` label, and the master's instructions were updated beforehand to honor an explicitly-given number rather than always auto-assigning — but the actual run still produced `VKAI-001`. Root cause not confirmed (possibly the updated `CLAUDE.md` wasn't yet in place on disk at the moment this particular run started). Not a blocking issue, but worth double-checking on the next story that explicit numbering is actually being honored.

**What happened, confirmed by direct human observation:**
1. `agent-vkai-master` read the story, determined it touched only the provider side (both API and frontend), and **asked clarifying questions** before proposing anything (confirmed directly — this was the key validation point for the whole design).
2. Human answered the questions; master proposed a plan (invoke `subAgent-vkai-provider-api`, then `subAgent-vkai-provider`, in that order since the frontend depends on the API's new field); human approved.
3. `subAgent-vkai-provider-api` added a `key` column via Prisma migration (with a data backfill for existing rows), implemented the generation algorithm (first letter of each name token, uppercased, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision) and returned it on create/list. It also **proactively** excluded `key` from the cross-cloud `GET /v1/catalog/policies` endpoint (an unprompted, correct security/scope judgment call, since that field should never leak to the client side's cache) — flagged this decision clearly in its report rather than making it silently. Committed to `dev`.
4. `subAgent-vkai-provider` added the locked `Key` field to the Add Plan form (revealed after save) and the `key` prefix to the catalog list display. Committed to `dev`.
5. Master logged the full outcome to `Story.md` and correctly reminded the human that both `dev`→`main` merges were still manual steps.
6. Human merged both PRs, redeployed to the live Azure VM (`git pull origin main` → `docker compose down` → `up --build -d`), confirmed the migration + backfill ran cleanly, and verified the whole flow live — both on existing catalog entries (retroactive key generation) and by creating a brand-new plan through the real UI (`Premium Gold Plan 2026` → `PGP2`). Also ran a fresh full E2E cross-cloud test afterward to confirm nothing regressed.

**Result:** first real, unscripted use of the orchestration system worked correctly end-to-end — ambiguity caught and asked about, human approval respected, correct subagent sequencing, correct repo-boundary discipline, a genuinely good unprompted judgment call on data exposure, and a clean, verifiable production outcome.

### 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03)

heading: 19.1 Design
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03) > ### 19.1 Design
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03) > ### 19.1 Design

Only the two API repos needed new pipeline work — the two frontend repos were already auto-deploying via Vercel's native GitHub integration (nothing to build there). The design deliberately keeps **one manual checkpoint** in an otherwise fully automated flow:

```
Story → agent-vkai-master → subagent(s) code, commit, push to dev
  → human reviews and merges dev → main   ← the only manual step
    → frontend repos: Vercel auto-deploys (pre-existing)
    → API repos: GitHub Actions auto-deploys via SSH (built this phase)
```

**Deliberately not automated:** the `dev` → `main` merge itself. Every merge across this whole project has been a manual, reviewed action; auto-merging was considered and rejected, since it removes the last human checkpoint before something goes live in production.

**Mechanism for the API repos:** a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) triggered on `push: branches: [main]`, using the `appleboy/ssh-action` to connect to the respective VM and run: `git pull origin main` → `docker compose down` → `docker compose up --build -d` → a health check. No separate step needed for Postgres (the container keeps running, its volume persists) or for schema migrations (already run automatically via `docker-entrypoint.sh`'s `prisma migrate deploy` on every container start — pre-existing behavior, not new).

heading: 19.2 SSH key setup
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03) > ### 19.2 SSH key setup
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03) > ### 19.2 SSH key setup

A **dedicated deploy keypair per VM** (not the owner's personal SSH key), so each cloud's automated access is fully independent of the other:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "github-actions-deploy-client-api" -f ~/.ssh/gh_actions_client_api_deploy -N ""
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "github-actions-deploy-provider-api" -f ~/.ssh/gh_actions_provider_api_deploy -N ""
```

Public keys appended to each VM's `authorized_keys` via a one-line piped SSH command; both keys manually verified with a direct SSH test **before** trusting GitHub Actions with them.

Each repo got 3 GitHub Actions secrets (`Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions`): `DEPLOY_HOST`, `DEPLOY_USER`, `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` (full private key contents, `BEGIN`/`END` lines included).

heading: 19.3 Debugging saga — three real issues, found and fixed in sequence
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03) > ### 19.3 Debugging saga — three real issues, found and fixed in sequence
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 19. Phase 6 — CI/CD Pipelines (2026-08-03) > ### 19.3 Debugging saga — three real issues, found and fixed in sequence

**Issue 1 — `~` doesn't expand.** The first workflow version used `cd ~/vkai-insurance-client-api`, which failed with "No such file or directory" even though the path was confirmed correct via a manual SSH session. Root cause: `~` doesn't reliably expand in `appleboy/ssh-action`'s non-interactive remote shell. **Fixed** by switching to the absolute path (`/home/vibhavkulshrestha/...`, `/home/vkaiadmin/...`).

**Issue 2 — wrong secret values (cross-repo mix-up).** After fixing the path, the *same* error persisted. Rather than guess again, temporary debug output was added to the workflow (`whoami`, `hostname`, `pwd`, directory listings) to see exactly what the pipeline's SSH session actually saw. This revealed the real cause immediately: the `hostname` printed was the **Azure provider VM**, not the GCP client VM — the `vkai-insurance-client-api` repo's `DEPLOY_HOST` secret had been set to the *provider's* IP by mistake during setup. **Fixed** by correcting the secret to the right IP; a follow-up auth failure after that (`DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` also mismatched) was fixed by re-pasting the correct key. **Lesson:** when a secret-backed pipeline fails identically after a code fix, verify the actual secret *values* directly rather than assuming the code is still wrong — a diagnostic pass (temporary debug output) found this in one run, versus further blind guessing.

**Issue 3 — health check too early (false failure).** Once path and secrets were correct, the deploy itself fully succeeded (visible in the logs — `git pull`, image rebuild, containers started) but the workflow still failed, on a `curl` returning `502`. Root cause: only a flat `sleep 5` before checking health — not enough time for Postgres's own healthcheck + Prisma migration + API boot to complete after a fresh `docker compose down/up`. **Fixed** by increasing the wait to `sleep 20` and replacing the single `curl` with a 5-attempt retry loop (5s apart), so a slightly slow boot doesn't fail the whole pipeline.

Both fixes (absolute path, wait+retry) were applied **proactively** to the provider-api repo's workflow from the start (rather than rediscovering them), and that pipeline went green on the first attempt.

Two things surfaced once the pipelines were live:

1. **The CI/CD pipeline itself was undocumented.** Both API repos' `README.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md` were updated to reflect that pushing to `main` now auto-deploys — including the two hard-won gotchas (absolute paths, health-check timing) and the required secrets, with the provider-api's `CLAUDE.md` explicitly warning not to copy-paste secret values from the sibling client-api repo (the exact mistake made during setup).
2. **A gap in the doc-update rule's own reach.** The "keep documentation current" standing rule (added in Phase 5, §18.5) had only been added to the 4 **subagent** definition files (`.claude/agents/*.md`), so it only applied when work was routed through `agent-vkai-master`. Since the CI/CD pipeline work was done by prompting Claude Code **directly** in each repo's own workspace (not through the master/subagent flow), that rule never applied — explaining why the pipeline wasn't auto-documented in the first place. **Fixed** by adding the same standing rule directly into each of the 4 repos' own `CLAUDE.md` files, so it now applies regardless of whether a change comes from direct prompting or from a subagent.

heading: 20.1 The story
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 20. VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation (2026-08-03) > ### 20.1 The story
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 20. VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation (2026-08-03) > ### 20.1 The story

`key` (added in VKAI-001) needed to flow through the full E2E system, including the client portal, for both existing and new records. This **deliberately reversed** a VKAI-001 decision: back then, a subagent proactively excluded `key` from the cross-cloud `GET /v1/catalog/policies` endpoint specifically so it would never reach the client. This story explicitly re-opened and reversed that call — a good example of a scope decision that was correct *at the time* but needed revisiting once real requirements evolved, and of documenting *why* a reversal is happening rather than just silently changing it.

Clarifying questions asked (and answered) before the master proposed a plan:
- Confirmed the reversal was intentional, not an oversight
- Scoped the prefix display to the Catalog page and the "Your policies"/dashboard list only — not nested premium/claim line items, since those already sit under a policy heading that would carry the prefix
- Confirmed existing (already-enrolled) records should update immediately via a forced sync, not wait on the natural staleness window

heading: 20.3 Two small gaps found during deployment (both fixed same day)
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 20. VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation (2026-08-03) > ### 20.3 Two small gaps found during deployment (both fixed same day)
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 20. VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation (2026-08-03) > ### 20.3 Two small gaps found during deployment (both fixed same day)

**Gap 1 — `scripts/` folder missing from the Docker image.** The new `refresh-catalog.js` script existed in the repo and ran fine locally, but `docker compose exec api npm run catalog:refresh` failed with `Cannot find module '/app/scripts/refresh-catalog.js'` once deployed. Root cause: same category of issue as the earlier `docker-compose.yml` env var gaps — the `Dockerfile`'s runtime stage explicitly lists which folders to `COPY` (`src`, `prisma`, etc.), and `scripts/` was simply never added to that list when the script was created. **Fixed** with one line (`COPY scripts ./scripts`), redeployed automatically via the CI/CD pipeline built in Phase 6.

**Gap 2 — a false alarm, not a real bug.** After deploying, a newly-created provider catalog entry ("New India Health Policy") didn't immediately appear in the client's catalog list. Before asking Claude Code to investigate, a manual `npm run catalog:refresh` was run as a diagnostic first — the entry appeared immediately, confirming this was just the normal 15-minute staleness window, not a defect. **Lesson reinforced:** always verify something is genuinely broken (e.g., "does a fresh force-refresh fix it?") before routing a fix request to Claude Code — saves a debugging cycle on what turns out to be expected behavior.

### 21. Phase 7 — Database Access & Ops Tooling (2026-08-09)

heading: 21.1 Purpose
breadcrumb: # VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 21. Phase 7 — Database Access & Ops Tooling (2026-08-09) > ### 21.1 Purpose
text:
# VKAI_INSURANCE_CLIENT_API_BASE_URL pointing to the live GCP client API's HTTPS URL > ## 21. Phase 7 — Database Access & Ops Tooling (2026-08-09) > ### 21.1 Purpose

Both production Postgres databases (client on GCP, provider on Azure) had never been accessed directly since going live — only through the applications themselves. This phase establishes the standing pattern for direct DB access, both via raw `psql` on the VM and via a GUI client (pgAdmin 4) tunneled from a local laptop, for ad-hoc inspection, debugging, and demo prep.

### 21.2 Direct `psql` access (on the VM itself)
```bash

heading: Client (GCP)
breadcrumb: # Client (GCP)
text:
# Client (GCP)

gcloud compute ssh vm-vkai-insurance-client-api-dev --project=vkai-insurance-dev --zone=us-central1-a
cd vkai-insurance-client-api
docker compose exec postgres psql -U postgres -d vkai_insurance_client_dev

heading: Provider (Azure)
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure)
text:
# Provider (Azure)

ssh vkaiadmin@20.80.90.33
cd vkai-insurance-provider-api
docker compose exec postgres psql -U postgres -d vkai_insurance_provider_dev
```

Table names are plain lowercase (`claims`, `policies`, `policy_catalog`, `premiums`, `users`, plus Prisma's own `_prisma_migrations`) — Prisma's camelCase model names map to snake_case at the DB level via `@@map`, consistent with the naming mismatch already noted in the "what/why recap" doc. No quoting needed for `\d` etc.

heading: 21.3 Key asymmetry — Postgres host ports differ between sides
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) > ### 21.3 Key asymmetry — Postgres host ports differ between sides
text:
# Provider (Azure) > ### 21.3 Key asymmetry — Postgres host ports differ between sides

**Not previously documented, and easy to trip over:** the two sides publish Postgres to different host ports.
- **Client (GCP):** `5432:5432`
- **Provider (Azure):** `5433:5432` — deliberately offset, per the provider API's own `.env` comment, to avoid a port clash if both stacks were ever run locally on one machine. This asymmetry is *not* mirrored in any diagram or the naming-conventions doc — worth remembering before assuming both sides behave identically.

heading: 21.4 GUI access via pgAdmin 4 (SSH tunnel pattern)

text:
# Provider (Azure) > ### 21.4 GUI access via pgAdmin 4 (SSH tunnel pattern)

```bash

# Client (GCP) — local 5433 -> VM's Postgres on 5432

gcloud compute ssh vm-vkai-insurance-client-api-dev --project=vkai-insurance-dev --zone=us-central1-a -- -L 5433:localhost:5432

# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3)

ssh -L 5434:localhost:5433 vkaiadmin@20.80.90.33
```

| | Client (GCP) | Provider (Azure) |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `localhost` | `localhost` |
| Port | `5433` | `5434` |
| Maintenance DB | `vkai_insurance_client_dev` | `vkai_insurance_provider_dev` |
| Username | `postgres` | `postgres` |
| Password | `postgres` | `postgres` |

heading: 21.5 Gotchas found during setup
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ### 21.5 Gotchas found during setup
text:
# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ### 21.5 Gotchas found during setup

- **Running the tunnel command from inside a VM instead of the local laptop.** If you're already SSH'd into one VM and run another `ssh -L ...` or `gcloud compute ssh ...` command from that shell, it executes remotely and doesn't create a usable local tunnel — it produces confusing errors (`Permission denied (publickey)`, `insufficient authentication scopes`) that look like an auth problem but are actually a "wrong machine" problem. Always confirm the shell prompt shows the local laptop, not a VM hostname, before starting a tunnel.
- **Assuming both sides use the same host port for Postgres.** They don't — see §21.3. Tunneling to the wrong remote port produces a misleading `server closed the connection unexpectedly` error in pgAdmin, rather than a clear "connection refused."
- **Copy-pasting field labels into pgAdmin's connection fields.** Pasting a value like `Host: localhost` (label included) into the Host field produces a DNS resolution error (`failed to resolve host 'Host: localhost'`) that has nothing to do with the tunnel or credentials — worth checking the literal field contents first if a "host not found" error appears despite the tunnel being confirmed up.

heading: 21.6 Security note (flagged, not yet acted on)
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ### 21.6 Security note (flagged, not yet acted on)
text:
# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ### 21.6 Security note (flagged, not yet acted on)

Both Postgres containers use the password `postgres` and publish their port to the VM's host network (not just the Docker network). Not internet-exposed (only 80/443 are open in each VM's firewall/NSG), so low urgency for a demo-scale project, but worth hardening (stronger password, drop the host port publish and rely on Docker network + SSH tunnel only) before this is used as a live client-facing demo rather than a personal build.

heading: 23.4 Diagram asset sourcing — a real lesson, not just a note
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 23. Phase 9 — Public Showcase Website (2026-08-12) > ### 23.4 Diagram asset sourcing — a real lesson, not just a note
text:
# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 23. Phase 9 — Public Showcase Website (2026-08-12) > ### 23.4 Diagram asset sourcing — a real lesson, not just a note

Initially attempted to reuse the insurance module's existing HTML/SVG diagram exports (`vkai-insurance-orchestration-flowchart-v1.html`, etc.) directly in the new site. Rendering these headlessly (via `wkhtmltoimage` and Playwright/Chromium, not just eyeballing a browser screenshot) surfaced **real, unresolved layout bugs** in the source HTML — not rendering artifacts:
- AI Orchestration diagram: right-side columns rendered clipped outside their declared canvas width; a fixed-height container silently truncated the Master Agent box's text, dropping step "6. Reminds the human" entirely; a label ("human reviews & merges") overlapped the branch box beneath it.
- System Flow diagram: minor label crowding around the cross-cloud sync column.

Freshly re-exported `.drawio`-native PNGs (provided directly by the user, not the HTML sources) were confirmed clean on inspection and used instead. **Decision: the showcase site displays static PNG exports of all three diagrams, not live HTML/SVG embeds** — simpler, avoids inheriting source-file layout bugs, and removes a runtime dependency (the architecture HTML's `viewer.diagrams.net` script tag, which fails to load without internet access and isn't a reliable thing to depend on in a deployed static site anyway).

heading: 23.5 Bugs found and root-caused during build
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 23. Phase 9 — Public Showcase Website (2026-08-12) > ### 23.5 Bugs found and root-caused during build
text:
# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 23. Phase 9 — Public Showcase Website (2026-08-12) > ### 23.5 Bugs found and root-caused during build

1. **Pointer-events trap**: the lightbox element remained in the DOM at `opacity:0` with `pointer-events:auto` because `.lightbox { display:flex }` overrode the browser's built-in `[hidden] { display:none }` (equal CSS specificity, author rule wins). It silently intercepted every click across the full viewport — Next button, diagrams, link cards — while keyboard navigation kept working normally (keyboard events don't hit-test). Confirmed via `document.elementFromPoint()` returning the lightbox div instead of the actual target. Fixed with explicit `[hidden] { display:none }` specificity rules plus a defensive `pointer-events:none` on the closed state.
2. **`:focus-visible` unreliable for programmatic `.focus()` calls**: JS moves focus to the active slide after navigation (for screen-reader accessibility). Relying on `:focus-visible` to suppress the resulting outline on mouse-driven navigation failed — Chrome's heuristic showed the ring anyway. Replaced with deterministic tracking: a `user-is-tabbing` class added to `<body>` on `Tab` keydown, removed on any `mousedown`/`touchstart`, with focus outlines gated behind `body.user-is-tabbing` in CSS instead of the pseudo-class.

Both were traced to root cause (not patched at the symptom level) and verified with actual mouse clicks and keyboard presses, not just code review.

heading: 23.6 Git identity incident
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 23. Phase 9 — Public Showcase Website (2026-08-12) > ### 23.6 Git identity incident

`vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md` — 40 scenarios in Advance Gherkin BDD (feature/scenario/background, data tables, `Scenario Outline` + `Examples` for boundary cases), organized into 10 modules:

| Module | Scenarios | Mix |
|---|---|---|
| Auth (Client Firebase + Provider Entra ID) | 8 | positive, negative, 1 boundary (email format) |
| Policy Catalog | 3 | browse, cache refresh, snapshot-isolation from catalog edits |
| Policy Enrollment & Activation | 5 | happy path, sync failure/retry, duplicate-event idempotency |
| Premium Payment | 4 | incl. boundary `Scenario Outline` on payment amount |
| Claims — Filing & Tracking (Client) | 6 | incl. boundary on claim amount vs. coverage limit |
| Claims — Review/Approval/Payout (Provider) | 6 | full Reviewer → Approver → Paid lifecycle, role-permission negative case |
| Policy Renewal | 2 | incl. boundary `Scenario Outline` on the 30-day expiry threshold |
| Consolidated Dashboard | 1 | single-call nested-history view |
| Cross-Cloud Sync & Resilience | 3 | failure isolation, background retry job, Sync Issues screen |
| End-to-End Journeys | 2 | full happy-path lifecycle; claim-rejected path |

ID scheme: `VJS-TC-<MODULE>-<NNN>` (e.g. `VJS-TC-CLM-004`), used as the Jira issue summary prefix for traceability back to this file. Tag scheme: layer (`@Client`/`@Provider`/`@Sync`), depth (`@E2E`/`@Regression`), type (`@Positive`/`@Negative`/`@Boundary`).

heading: 25.3 A hard architectural blocker, correctly identified rather than worked around
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 25. Phase 11 — Test Automation Framework: Selenium/Cucumber/TestNG (2026-08-13) > ### 25.3 A hard architectural blocker, correctly identified rather than worked around
text:
# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 25. Phase 11 — Test Automation Framework: Selenium/Cucumber/TestNG (2026-08-13) > ### 25.3 A hard architectural blocker, correctly identified rather than worked around

The original pilot target was `VJS-TC-E2E-001` (full happy path, including provider Approver actions: activate policy, approve claim, mark paid). Investigation surfaced a **real, structural blocker**, not a workaround-able inconvenience:

1. **Microsoft Entra ID Security Defaults is Enabled tenant-wide**, and the dedicated Approver QA account has **no MFA method registered** — meaning the very next login would force MFA enrollment, which Selenium cannot complete.
2. This also **rules out the MSAL ROPC token-bypass route** — Microsoft explicitly blocks ROPC when Security Defaults or Conditional Access MFA is enforced.
3. Direct investigation of `vkai-insurance-provider-api`'s route code (read-only, no changes made) confirmed the Approver-action endpoints (`POST /v1/policies/:id/activate`, `/v1/claims/:id/approve`, `/v1/claims/:id/mark-paid`) are **exclusively Entra-JWT-gated** (`entraAuth` + `requireRole('Approver')`) — the shared-secret `X-VKAI-Sync-Key` mechanism only covers cross-cloud create/read routes, not status transitions. No API-key or service-account path exists for these actions as the system is built today.

**Decision made:** provider Approver actions (activate, approve, reject, mark-paid) stay **manual/exploratory testing**, tagged `@Manual` in feature files — same posture already established for the backend-only sync scenarios (§24, VJS-37/38). `VJS-TC-E2E-001` was re-scoped into an automatable slice (enroll → Pending → premium-payment-blocked) plus a documented-but-excluded `@Manual` leg (activate → pay → claim → approve → paid).

**Deferred, not rejected:** a deliberate, security-reviewed test seam on `vkai-insurance-provider-api` (an env-gated, non-prod-only affordance for a scoped test credential) remains the theoretically "correct" long-term fix if full E2E automation of the provider leg becomes a priority — flagged as a future enhancement, out of scope for this phase since it's a change to a live production API.

Every locator was built from **real, observed DOM** — headings/buttons/testids summaries or full `#root` innerHTML captured live from the browser console, never guessed from the business-flows spec alone. This caught two things that would otherwise have produced silently-wrong tests:
- A DOM capture accidentally taken from the **provider (ops) portal** instead of the client portal was caught immediately (branding, nav, and control differences were unambiguous) before any Page Object was built against it.
- The pending-policy status text was case-sensitive (`pending`, not `Pending`) — the first live run correctly failed on this exact, pre-flagged risk; fixed by locating on the status CSS class rather than literal text, then reconfirmed green.

breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 25. Phase 11 — Test Automation Framework: Selenium/Cucumber/TestNG (2026-08-13) > ### 25.6 Credential handling

Environment-variable-first, gitignored-local-file fallback — the same key names work in both places, so nothing changes between local runs and CI:
- `ConfigReader` checks `System.getenv()` first, falls back to `config-local.properties` (gitignored; `config-local.properties.example` with placeholder keys only is committed)
- In CI, the same keys (`VKAI_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `VKAI_CLIENT_PASSWORD`) are set as **GitHub Actions repository secrets** via `gh secret set`, injected as env vars
- Dedicated QA test accounts were created manually (not scripted) on both sides — a Firebase account on the client portal, and an Entra ID account in the `VKAI-Insurance-Provider-Approvers` group on the provider portal — kept separate from the personal `vkailabs@gmail.com` / `vkailabs@outlook.com` identities used elsewhere in this project
- **Test-data accumulation accepted (Option A):** each automated run creates a real pending policy on the live client dev DB; since it's a dedicated QA account and activation stays manual, this pollution is accepted rather than building a cleanup path — revisit only if a future scenario needs an exact policy count

# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 25. Phase 11 — Test Automation Framework: Selenium/Cucumber/TestNG (2026-08-13) > ### 25.10 Scope-down decision: UI-automation-only, finalized at 10 scenarios (2026-08-14)

Two Batches (2 and 3) were completed after §25.1–25.9 were written, closing out category ① (catalog, claims-pending negative) and category ③ (registration, via a Gmail-plus-addressing dynamic-email helper with a safety guard against submitting the wrong email). This brought the automated count to **10 scenarios (12 execution rows)**, with only category ② (9 scenarios, gated on the provider-fixture-seam spec) still open.

At that point, a deliberate instruction was given to **stop pursuing category ②** and instead **lock the regression pack's scope permanently to UI-only, no-API, no-manual automation** — explicitly ruling out both remaining paths that could have closed the gap (the fixture seam for API-level provider actions, and tracking provider actions as a manual/exploratory checklist). This is a scope decision, not an unfinished item:

- **`vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md` was rewritten** to contain only the 10 kept scenarios, with a "Scope Change" section documenting the rationale (the Entra ID Security Defaults + no-MFA-exempt-account blocker from §25.3, plus the explicit no-API/no-manual instruction) and per-scenario `NOTE:` comments recording every spec-vs-reality wording mismatch found along the way (AUTH-002's actual error text, AUTH-003's `user@domain` HTML5-validity gotcha, AUTH-005's already-reconciled wording).
- **The other 30 Jira issues were labeled `descoped` first**, then — after review — **permanently deleted from Jira** (not just labeled) at the user's explicit direction. Verified via JQL (`project = VJS AND labels = descoped` → 0 remaining after deletion).
- **A specific request to cover the full provider-inclusive E2E lifecycle** (provider creates/activates a policy, client pays, provider reviews the payment, client files a claim, provider takes it through review → approve → mark-paid, with client-side status verification at each step) **was evaluated and declined** — both on the structural MFA/API grounds already established, and because using the personal/admin Entra account instead of a QA account was raised and correctly rejected: Security Defaults is tenant-wide, not account-specific, so it would not have bypassed the blocker, and would have introduced real credential-exposure risk (admin password in CI secrets/config) for no actual gain.
- **`docs/TRIAGE.md`** in the automation repo was flagged for a follow-up correction (via Claude Code, not yet confirmed complete as of this log entry) — it was written when category ②'s unlock was still an active plan and needs updating to reflect that the roadmap it describes is closed, not pending.

**Net effect:** `vkai-insurance-automation` and `vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md` are now in full agreement — 10 scenarios, both fully green in CI and fully described in the pack, with no gap between "what's documented" and "what's built." This is considered the **stable, final state** of the regression automation effort unless a future, deliberate decision reopens the API-automation or manual-testing question.

heading: 26.2 The two new subagents
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 26. Phase 12 — Orchestration Expansion: QA Subagents (2026-08-15) > ### 26.2 The two new subagents

# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 26. Phase 12 — Orchestration Expansion: QA Subagents (2026-08-15) > ### 26.2 The two new subagents

**`agent-vkai-automation`** — scoped to `vkai-insurance-automation` only (plus read access to the two companion regression docs). Story flow: reads the new story → decides if UI-automatable test cases are needed (UI-only, no API/manual/DB — same scope-lock as `docs/TRIAGE.md`) → if none apply, says so and stops → writes new Gherkin, updates `vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md` → builds the automation using the framework's existing live-DOM-only-locator discipline → updates `vkai-insurance-regression-automation-v1.md` if the stack/scope changed → **stops and requires explicit user confirmation that all 4 app repos are merged `dev → main`** before running anything against the live environment → on confirmation, executes and produces an ExtentReport → hands a structured summary to `agent-vkai-jira-update`. Never touches Jira directly, never edits `Story.md`, never touches the other 4 repos.

**`agent-vkai-jira-update`** — scoped to Jira operations only, via direct REST API calls (not the chat-based Atlassian Rovo connector, which isn't reachable from Claude Code). Creates new Test Case issues from the automation agent's handoff, transitions them to Done post-execution, and attaches the ExtentReport. Tools locked to `Read, Bash, Grep, Glob` — no `Write`/`Edit`, reinforcing it can never touch repo code.

Both are invoked **explicitly, last, in sequence**, by the user acting as master — not autonomously triggered. Neither writes to `Story.md`; per the existing append-only convention, only `agent-vkai-master` does, after both report back.

Three keys, added in two passes (a gap was caught and closed the same day): `VKAI_JIRA_EMAIL`, `VKAI_JIRA_API_TOKEN`, and `VKAI_JIRA_BASE_URL` (added after the agent's first live test revealed it was inferring the Jira site from a naming-conventions doc reference rather than reading it from config — fixed to read explicitly and stop-and-ask if unset, rather than silently guess).

**Verified working:** a read-only smoke test (`GET` on `VJS-2`) returned `HTTP 200` with correct issue data (summary, type, status, labels, component) — confirming the token, email, and base URL are all correctly wired before any real story depends on it.

heading: 26.4 Incident: a real credential got overwritten mid-setup
breadcrumb: # Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 26. Phase 12 — Orchestration Expansion: QA Subagents (2026-08-15) > ### 26.4 Incident: a real credential got overwritten mid-setup
text:
# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 26. Phase 12 — Orchestration Expansion: QA Subagents (2026-08-15) > ### 26.4 Incident: a real credential got overwritten mid-setup

While adding the two new Jira keys to the local `config-local.properties`, a `cp` (copy-template-over-real-file) command was run **after** confirming the real file already existed — the exact case the setup steps said to skip. This silently reverted three fields (`VKAI_CLIENT_BASE_URL`, `VKAI_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `VKAI_CLIENT_PASSWORD`) to placeholder values, wiping the working client QA credentials. Caught immediately (the user checked the file contents before assuming success), and fixed by manually re-entering the three real values from the client portal's existing QA account — no credential rotation was needed since the *value* wasn't exposed, just overwritten locally. Logged as a reminder: destructive-by-default commands (`cp` over an existing file, with no confirmation prompt) are a real risk even in a careful workflow, and "check before running" is easy to skip under momentum.

# Provider (Azure) — local 5434 -> VM's Postgres on 5433 (note the offset, per §21.3) > ## 26. Phase 12 — Orchestration Expansion: QA Subagents (2026-08-15) > ### 26.9 Doc-drift incident and fix (2026-08-15)

After VKAI-005 completed, `agent-vkai-automation` updated the two companion regression docs — but only in the **local, non-git-tracked `context/` folder** used to bundle reference material for Claude Code sessions, not in this Claude Project's knowledge base (which has no mechanism for Claude Code to push into). This created real drift, caught by the user re-checking rather than assuming, on re-upload:

- Both `AUTH-006` and `DASH-001` still carried `"(VKAI-005 - new)"` placeholder text instead of their actual Jira keys (`VJS-42`, `VJS-43`) — the docs were written *before* the Jira agent ran and never got a follow-up pass after.
- The regression pack's "Scope Change" section still asserted "the 10 scenarios below are the entire active regression pack going forward" — stale the moment the pack grew to 13.
- The automation reference doc's §8 heading read "Scope: deliberately closed at 10" directly above a §7 table showing 12 live scenarios — self-contradictory on its face.

All three were corrected (this Project's copies, 2026-08-15): real Jira keys substituted throughout, the scope-change language reworded to distinguish the *permanent boundary* (UI-only, no API/manual, no provider actions) from the *scenario count* (expected to grow within that boundary), and §8's heading/framing corrected to match §7 rather than contradict it. **A standing instruction was also given to retrain the subagents** so this class of drift — real Jira keys never backfilled, scope language going stale as the pack grows — doesn't recur on future stories (see `agent-vkai-automation`'s definition for the added step).

**Process fix confirmed shipped (2026-08-15), same day:** rather than a one-off correction, the root cause was fixed in the agent definitions themselves.
- `agent-vkai-jira-update` now must return an explicit scenario-ID → Jira-key mapping for every issue it creates — "created successfully" is no longer an acceptable handoff.
- `agent-vkai-automation` is now a documented **two-pass** agent: pass one writes only greppable placeholders (`(<STORY-ID> - new)`), never a guessed Jira key; a new "final doc-reconciliation pass" runs *after* the Jira agent reports back — swapping every placeholder for its real key, grep-verifying none remain, and refreshing stale count/scope language.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s orchestration sequence now explicitly ends `...→ automation (build+run) → jira (report real keys) → automation (final reconciliation)`, with a new Hard Rule (#10): never end a story with placeholder keys still in the two regression docs, and always end the user-facing summary with a re-upload reminder when those `context/`-only docs changed.

This was treated as a process/tooling fix to the agent framework itself, not a product story — no `VKAI-XXX` number assigned, logged instead as a `Story.md` QA-Audit-Log entry, consistent with how the original 6-subagent setup was recorded.

**Companion to:** `vkai-insurance-test-automation-architecture-v1.drawio` (diagram), `vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md` (the Gherkin *what*), `vkai-insurance-regression-automation-v1.md` (framework *how-it-works* reference), `vkai-insurance-setup-log.md` §11, §24–27 (the chronological story)

heading: 1. Purpose and how to read this document
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 1. Purpose and how to read this document
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 1. Purpose and how to read this document

This is the architecture-level counterpart to the solution/technical architecture diagram already held in this Project (`vkai-insurance-solution-architecture-v2.drawio`). Where that diagram shows how the client and provider portals, APIs, and databases fit together, this one shows how the platform *proves those systems work* — the testing framework's structure, the AI agents that operate it, and the boundary of what it deliberately does and does not cover.

The architecture is organized into six layers, top to bottom in the diagram, matching the order information actually flows through the system: requirements come in from Jira and a Gherkin source-of-truth file, an AI orchestration layer decides what to build and gates every live run on human approval, a Java/Maven test framework does the actual browser automation, that framework runs either on a laptop or in CI, both point at the same live production client portal, and results flow back out through a reporting layer into Jira. A permanent architectural boundary and a credential strategy sit alongside as constraints that shape every layer above them, not as a seventh layer.

---

heading: 2. Layer 1 — Requirement & Traceability Layer
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 2. Layer 1 — Requirement & Traceability Layer
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 2. Layer 1 — Requirement & Traceability Layer

Four artifacts anchor the whole system so that "what should be tested," "what is tested," and "what actually happened" never drift apart silently.

**Jira Cloud, project `VJS`.** Two issue types matter here: `Test Case`, one per automated scenario, holding the Gherkin block in its Description field for traceability back to the source file; and `Story`, added in Phase 13 specifically so a plain Jira issue — not pasted chat text — is the single entry point for a unit of work. Every `Test Case` issue is summary-prefixed with its scenario ID (`VJS-TC-<MODULE>-<NNN>`) so a Jira key and a Gherkin scenario can always be matched by eye.

**`vkai-insurance-regression-test-pack-v1.md`.** The Gherkin source of truth. Every `.feature` file in the automation repo is ported near-verbatim from this document, not written independently — if the two ever disagree, this file wins and the `.feature` file is corrected, never the other way around. It currently holds 15 scenarios (13 automated, 2 held `@Manual`), each carrying inline `NOTE:` comments wherever a spec assumption turned out to be wrong against the live app (exact error text, HTML5 validation quirks, and so on), so those corrections are visible in place rather than buried in commit history.

**`vkai-insurance-regression-automation-v1.md`.** The technical reference — tech stack, project layout, credential strategy, the architectural blocker, and the extension rules. Read this before touching the repo; read the setup log if you want the story behind a specific decision.

**`Story.md`.** An append-only log living at the orchestration root (`~/vkai-labs/insurance/Story.md`), carrying both the internal `VKAI-XXX` sequence number and the corresponding Jira Story key side by side, plus a separate "QA Audit Log" section for orchestration runs that weren't tied to a numbered story (process fixes, standalone QA-tail runs).

---

heading: 3. Layer 2 — AI Orchestration Layer (7 Claude Code subagents, human-gated)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 3. Layer 2 — AI Orchestration Layer (7 Claude Code subagents, human-gated)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 3. Layer 2 — AI Orchestration Layer (7 Claude Code subagents, human-gated)

This is the layer that turns "a Jira Story key" into "code shipped, tests run, results reported" without a human ever re-typing requirements or manually reconciling Jira. It sits one level above all five application/automation repos, at `~/vkai-labs/insurance/`.

`agent-vkai-master` is the orchestrator. It reads a Story (fetched by `agent-vkai-jira-story`, never pasted), determines which of the four application subagents plus the QA tail are needed and in what dependency-aware order, asks clarifying questions on any real ambiguity rather than guessing, and — critically — presents a plan and **waits for explicit human approval** before invoking anything. Every subagent starts with a fresh context window and no visibility into the master's own conversation, so the master must pass all necessary context explicitly on each invocation.

Two subagents are specific to the test framework and are the ones this architecture diagram focuses on:

- **`agent-vkai-automation`** is scoped to `vkai-insurance-automation` only, plus read access to the two regression docs. Given a story, it decides whether any newly-needed coverage is UI-automatable within the permanent scope boundary (§6); if not, it says so and stops rather than reaching for API or manual workarounds. If it is, it authors new Gherkin, updates the regression test pack, builds the automation using the framework's live-DOM-only locator discipline, and then **stops and requires an explicit human confirmation that all four application repos are merged `dev → main`** before running anything against the live environment. It never touches Jira directly and never edits `Story.md`.
- **`agent-vkai-jira-update`** is scoped to Jira operations only, via direct REST calls (the chat-based Atlassian connector isn't reachable from Claude Code). It creates new `Test Case` issues from the automation agent's handoff, transitions them to Done after a run, and attaches the ExtentReport. Its tools are locked to `Read, Bash, Grep, Glob` — no `Write`/`Edit` — so it structurally cannot touch repo code.

A third, added in Phase 13, brackets every story rather than running mid-sequence: **`agent-vkai-jira-story`** is the sole subagent permitted to write to a parent Story issue. MODE 1 ("fetch") parses the Story's `Given/When/Then` description, transitions it to In Progress, and hands the scenarios to the master. MODE 2 ("close"), invoked last after the QA tail reports back, posts a structured summary comment, links each new `Test Case` to the Story via a `Relates` link, and transitions the Story to Done.

A standing **human gate** sits between the automation agent's build step and any live run: the merge confirmation described above, plus a second confirmation of the exact Jira write-target keys before `agent-vkai-jira-update` is allowed to touch anything. Nothing in this pipeline writes to production Jira or runs against the live portal without an explicit human "go."

---

heading: 4. Layer 3 — Test Automation Framework (`vkai-insurance-automation`, Java 17 / Maven)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 4. Layer 3 — Test Automation Framework (`vkai-insurance-automation`, Java 17 / Maven)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 4. Layer 3 — Test Automation Framework (`vkai-insurance-automation`, Java 17 / Maven)

This is the framework itself, read top-to-bottom as it actually executes:

**BDD layer — Cucumber-JVM 7.20.1.** `.feature` files under `src/test/resources/features/`, one file per module (auth, catalog, enrollment, premium, e2e), holding Gherkin ported from the regression pack.

**Test execution layer — TestNG 7.10.2.** `RegressionRunner` wires Cucumber to TestNG (via `cucumber-testng`) rather than JUnit5, a deliberate choice for native parallel/data-provider support. The runner's tag filter is `@Client and not @Manual`, which is what actually enforces the scope boundary at execution time — the two held scenarios (`DASH-002`, `DASH-004`) are tagged `@Manual` specifically so they're excluded from every real run without needing to be deleted. Dependency injection between step-definition classes is handled by PicoContainer (`cucumber-picocontainer`), sharing a `WebDriver` and test state without static fields.

**Step definition layer.** `AuthSteps`, `EnrollmentSteps`, `PremiumSteps` — a small, deliberately reused set of step classes rather than one class per feature file, since most Gherkin phrasing across modules maps onto the same handful of user actions (log in, view dashboard, enroll, attempt payment).

**Page Object Model layer.** `BasePage` plus one page class per screen (`ClientLoginPage`, `SignupPage`, `CatalogPage`, `DashboardPage`), isolating Selenium locators from step logic so a markup change touches one file, not every scenario that exercises that screen.

**Core utilities layer.** `ConfigReader` (environment-variable-first, falls back to a gitignored local properties file — see §7), `DriverFactory`, `WaitUtils`, and `TestData` (a dynamic Gmail plus-addressing helper for non-idempotent flows like registration, with a safety guard that validates every signup submission against the configured QA email pattern before it's ever sent, added after a real personal email was accidentally used once during manual DOM-capture work).

**UI automation engine — Selenium 4.27.0.** Selenium Manager handles driver binaries directly, so there's no separate WebDriverManager dependency. The governing discipline at this layer, applied to every locator in the framework without exception, is that **nothing is built from assumed markup** — every locator traces back to a real, live DOM capture (browser console `#root` innerHTML or a summarized headings/buttons/testids snapshot), because the client app has no `data-testid` attributes anywhere. This caught two real defects before they shipped: a DOM capture once came from the wrong portal entirely (provider instead of client), and a status locator built on literal text (`"Pending"`) failed its first live run because the actual rendered class-based state text was lowercase (`"pending"`) — both fixed by trusting the live app over the spec, and by preferring CSS-class locators over text matches for anything state-dependent.

---

heading: 5. Layer 4 — Execution Environments
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 5. Layer 4 — Execution Environments
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 5. Layer 4 — Execution Environments

Two execution paths share identical code and identical credential key names, so a scenario behaves the same whether it's run by a person or by CI.

**Local execution** — `mvn test` on a developer machine, reading `config-local.properties` (gitignored; a placeholder-only `.example` file is the committed template).

**CI execution** — GitHub Actions, `ubuntu-latest`, with headless Chrome available out of the box (no Docker layer was judged necessary; that decision is explicitly revisit-if-cross-browser-testing-becomes-a-priority, not permanent). The workflow triggers on **pull_request to `dev`/`main`** plus `workflow_dispatch` for on-demand runs — deliberately *not* on every push to `dev`, specifically to bound how much test-data churn each automated run adds to the live portal's database. Credentials arrive as GitHub Actions repository secrets (`VKAI_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `VKAI_CLIENT_PASSWORD`) under the same key names `ConfigReader` already expects locally.

---

heading: 6. Layer 5 — System Under Test, and the Permanent Architectural Boundary
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 6. Layer 5 — System Under Test, and the Permanent Architectural Boundary
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 6. Layer 5 — System Under Test, and the Permanent Architectural Boundary

Every test in this framework runs against the **live, deployed** client portal (`https://vkai-insurance-client.vercel.app`) — never a local build, never a staging environment — using a dedicated Firebase QA account kept separate from personal identities.

The provider portal is structurally out of reach, and this is the single most consequential architectural fact governing the whole framework. Microsoft Entra ID Security Defaults is enabled tenant-wide, and the dedicated Approver QA account has no MFA method registered — any login attempt, automated or manual, risks triggering forced MFA enrollment, which Selenium cannot complete. This also rules out an MSAL ROPC token-bypass, since Microsoft blocks ROPC outright when Security Defaults or Conditional Access MFA is enforced. Read-only investigation of the provider API's route code confirmed the Approver-action endpoints (`activate`, `approve`, `reject`, `mark-paid`) are exclusively Entra-JWT-gated with no service-account or API-key path — so there is no seam to automate through even if the login problem were solved.

Three ways of closing this gap were each considered and explicitly declined, not merely left undone: an env-gated fixture-seam on the provider API (would constitute API-level test automation), tracking provider actions as a manual/exploratory checklist (would constitute manual scenario tracking), and using a personal/admin Entra account instead of a QA account (Security Defaults is tenant-wide, not account-specific, so it wouldn't have bypassed anything — and would have introduced real credential-exposure risk for no benefit). The resulting **permanent boundary** is: UI-automation only, client-side, no API-level test automation, no manual/exploratory scenario tracking, no provider/Entra actions. Of the original 40 regression scenarios, 30 fell inside that excluded territory and were deliberately deleted from Jira (not deferred, not labeled-and-kept) once the boundary was locked in.

What is *not* frozen is the scenario count within that boundary — new genuinely-UI-only client scenarios are expected to keep being added as stories ship (13 automated today, up from the original 10, plus 2 more authored-but-held pending a reproducible data state). Anything proposed from the deleted 30 is not a "just add it" request; it requires consciously reopening §6's decision with the same trade-off conversation, not quietly building toward it.

---

heading: 7. Credential & Configuration Strategy
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 7. Credential & Configuration Strategy
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 7. Credential & Configuration Strategy

One pattern, applied identically everywhere: **environment variable first, gitignored local-file fallback**, with the same key names in every context. `ConfigReader` checks `System.getenv()` first, then falls back to `config-local.properties` (gitignored; never committed). Locally that file holds real values; in CI, GitHub Actions repository secrets are injected as environment variables under the same names, so no code path needs to know which environment it's running in.

Only one QA credential set exists in this framework: a dedicated Firebase account on the client portal. No provider or Entra QA credentials are used anywhere in this repo — consistent with §6's boundary, there is nothing here that would need them. Test-data accumulation (a real pending policy per enrollment run, a real Firebase account per registration run) is an accepted trade-off, not a defect: this is a dedicated QA-only account, so pollution has no real-world cost, and no cleanup automation exists or is planned.

---

heading: 8. Layer 6 — Reporting & Feedback Loop
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 8. Layer 6 — Reporting & Feedback Loop
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 8. Layer 6 — Reporting & Feedback Loop

Every run produces an ExtentReports 5.1.2 report via the Grasshopper Cucumber7 adapter, written to `reports/spark/index.html` with screenshots auto-attached on failure. From there the two Jira-facing subagents close the loop: `agent-vkai-jira-update` attaches the report to each affected `Test Case` issue and transitions it to Done (only after the human-confirmed write-target gate in §3), and `agent-vkai-jira-story` (MODE 2) posts a summary comment on the parent Story, links every new `Test Case` via a `Relates` relationship, and transitions the Story itself to Done. A known, low-priority gap: attached reports are the bare `index.html`, whose Spark styling depends on sibling assets in `reports/spark/` that aren't attached alongside it, so a report viewed detached from a full report folder may render unstyled — the content is intact, and zipping the whole folder is a flagged future fix, not yet actioned.

---

heading: 9. What this architecture deliberately does not claim
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 9. What this architecture deliberately does not claim
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 9. What this architecture deliberately does not claim

This framework proves the **client-side UI**, end to end, against production, on every PR into `dev`/`main` and on demand. It does not claim coverage of the provider portal, of any API surface directly, of cross-cloud sync behavior, or of any scenario requiring an Entra ID login — all of that remains either exercised implicitly by the solution architecture's own production usage or, for the provider Approver flows specifically, untested by this pipeline until a future, deliberate decision reopens §6. Anyone extending this framework should read that section before assuming a gap is simply unfinished work.

---

heading: 10. Pointers
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance — Test Automation Architecture v1 > ## 10. Pointers

heading: Accounts & Identities
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Accounts & Identities
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Accounts & Identities

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub org | Used existing `vkailabs` org, created 4 repos, all public | GitHub Free only enforces branch protection on public repos; this is a portfolio/demo project anyway, so public visibility was an acceptable trade |
| GitHub identity gotcha | Discovered `vkailabs` org is owned by a separate `vkailabs@gmail.com` GitHub account, not your personal `VibhavKul` account | Explains why `git push` failed with 403 even though repos were visible — added `VibhavKul` as collaborator on all 4 repos to fix |
| Azure account | Created dedicated `vkailabs@outlook.com` Microsoft account | Azure/Entra ID is cleaner tied to a native Microsoft account — avoids messy identity aliasing |
| Azure signup 403 | Signup failed via desktop browser/cards, succeeded via mobile Safari | Root cause likely browser/network/IP reputation issue, not the cards themselves |
| GCP account | Used existing `vkailabs@gmail.com` | No new identity needed — GCP doesn't require a dedicated account the way Azure benefits from one |
| Firebase project | Created `vkai-insurance-client` under `vkailabs@gmail.com`, enabled Email/Password auth | Needed a customer-facing identity provider for the client side |
| Entra ID app registration | Created `VKAI Insurance Provider Portal` — single-tenant SPA, redirect URI `localhost:5174`, exposed API scope `access_as_user`, 2 security groups (Reviewers/Approvers) | Needed an ops-facing identity provider for the provider side; single app registration used for both the SPA and API for simplicity |
| Vercel | Connected via GitHub OAuth, Hobby (free) plan | Personal/non-commercial demo project — Hobby tier is free and sufficient |

heading: Cloud & Architecture Decisions
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Cloud & Architecture Decisions
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Cloud & Architecture Decisions

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud split | Client side = 100% GCP; Provider side = 100% Azure | Deliberate dual-cloud split (not "use both somewhere") — demonstrates genuine multi-cloud competency, gives two different infra patterns to discuss in interviews |
| No shared database | Client and provider each own an independent Postgres instance; no cross-cloud DB access | Matches the "fully independent" requirement at the data layer, not just the code layer |
| Cross-cloud sync | Direct HTTPS calls at time of action, not a message queue | Simpler and cheaper for this demo's scale; a queue (Pub/Sub ↔ Service Bus) is a viable future upgrade, not needed now |
| Sync retry | `sync_status` field (pending/synced/failed) + `sync_attempts` counter on each record; background cron job retries every 5 min, capped at 5 attempts | Cross-cloud calls can fail transiently (network blips); records shouldn't be lost, just retried — **confirmed working live** when a genuinely failed enrollment was auto-recovered by the retry job |
| Sync idempotency | Every sync call carries a unique `event_id`; receiving side checks it before processing | Prevents duplicate records if a retry succeeds after a slow-but-actually-successful original call — **confirmed working live** during duplicate-delivery testing |
| Service-to-service auth | Shared secret sent via `X-VKAI-Sync-Key` header | Simple to implement/demo; sufficient for a portfolio project's threat model |
| Client auth | Firebase Authentication / Identity Platform | GCP's native customer-identity service; corrected from an earlier mistaken plan to use "Active Directory" (a Microsoft/Azure-only concept) |
| Provider auth | Entra ID (Azure AD), individual logins per ops user | Preserves a per-user audit trail (who approved/rejected what) — real-world practice, not just a demo nicety |
| Provider roles | `Reviewer` (move to Under Review) and `Approver` (approve/reject/mark paid) | Matches the basic scope requested; both roles see everything, differ only in allowed actions |
| Policy model | Provider defines a catalog; client browses and enrolls (no client-side custom policies) | Simpler and more realistic — matches how real insurers actually operate |
| Claims flow | `Submitted → Under Review → Approved/Rejected → Paid` | Standard, minimal state machine; **verified working live through all 3 transitions** |
| Renewal | Self-service — client extends `expiry_date` directly, no ops approval | It's a renewal of an already-approved policy, not a new one — approval step would be redundant |
| Claim workflow gating | Flexible — an Approver can act without a Reviewer touching it first | Single generic ops workflow for the basic scope; can be tightened later if desired |
| Sync issues view | Added a provider-side screen showing permanently-failed syncs | Visibility for ops without digging through logs; **proved genuinely useful** — caught real failed syncs live during this project's own debugging session |

heading: Database & Data Model
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Database & Data Model
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Database & Data Model

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| Two independent schemas | Client DB and provider DB each model policy/premium/claim from their own side | Matches "fully independent" at the data layer; linked only via synced foreign references, not real cross-DB foreign keys |
| DB hosting | Postgres running in a Docker container on the API VM, not a managed DB service | GCP Cloud SQL and Azure SQL Database aren't in either cloud's Always Free tier; self-hosted Postgres keeps cost at zero |
| `sync_status` inline | Kept on each syncable record directly, no separate `sync_log` audit table | Simpler schema for a demo; retry job only needs to query `WHERE sync_status IN ('pending','failed')` |
| `sync_attempts` / `event_id` | Added to `policies`/`premiums`/`claims` during actual Phase 3 build (beyond the original Phase 2 ERD) | The ERD showed the retry/idempotency *concept* but was missing the concrete fields needed to actually implement it |
| Prisma camelCase | Confirmed that Prisma model field names (`premiumAmount`, `isActive`, `enrolledAt`) flow straight through into JSON API responses with no transformation layer | Explains why several integration bugs were naming mismatches — any consuming code has to expect camelCase, not the `snake_case` used at the raw DB column level |

heading: Tech Stack
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Tech Stack
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Tech Stack

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| React (Vite) | Chosen over Create React App for the frontend | Faster dev server, more modern tooling, standard choice for new React projects |
| Node.js + Express | Backend API framework | Lightweight, standard, pairs well with the rest of the stack |
| Prisma | ORM for Postgres access | Type-safe queries, handles migrations cleanly, widely used and easy to demo |
| Docker + Docker Compose | Containerized both the API and Postgres for local dev | Reproducible local environment; same container pattern will carry into VM deployment later |
| Firebase Admin SDK | Used server-side (client API) to verify customer JWTs | The API needs to independently verify tokens issued by Firebase Auth — separate from the public web SDK used in the frontend |
| MSAL (`@azure/msal-browser` + `@azure/msal-react`) | Used client-side (provider frontend) for Entra ID login | Microsoft's official auth library, matches the Entra ID app registration setup |
| `jsonwebtoken` + `jwks-rsa` | Used server-side (provider API) to verify Entra ID JWTs against Microsoft's JWKS endpoint | Manual JWKS validation approach for the v2 Azure AD token contract |
| node-cron | Powers the background sync retry job on both APIs | Simple, no extra infrastructure (like a real job queue) needed for a demo-scale retry mechanism |
| pino | Structured JSON logging library, used on both APIs | Matches the naming doc's required structured log fields (timestamp, env, service, correlationId, level, message) |
| Nginx + Let's Encrypt | Planned reverse proxy + TLS for both API VMs (not yet configured — still local dev) | Demonstrates manual TLS/reverse-proxy setup rather than relying solely on managed PaaS TLS termination — a deliberate interview talking point |
| CORS (`cors` npm package) | Added to the client API after hitting a browser block; included from the start on the provider API | Browsers block cross-origin requests by default; lesson from the client API's follow-up fix was successfully applied proactively on the provider build |

heading: Build Progress & Fixes — All 4 Repos
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Build Progress & Fixes — All 4 Repos
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Build Progress & Fixes — All 4 Repos

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| `vkai-insurance-client-api` | Built, containerized, tested, pushed — all cross-cloud sync paths verified working | First repo — backend the frontend depends on, built first |
| `vkai-insurance-client` | Built (auth, dashboard, catalog, policy detail), tested, pushed | Matching frontend for the client API |
| `vkai-insurance-provider-api` | Built, containerized, tested, pushed — all cross-cloud sync paths verified working | Backend for the ops/provider side |
| `vkai-insurance-provider` | Built (MSAL auth, catalog, enrollments, claims, premiums, sync-issues, role-based UI), tested, pushed | Matching frontend for the provider API |
| Docker port conflict | Killed a leftover local `node` process holding port 4000 | A stray process from earlier local testing was blocking the container from binding the port |
| Firebase private key formatting | Fixed by keeping the key on one line, `\n` as literal text, wrapped in quotes | JSON's escaped `\n` sequences get mangled into real line breaks during careless copy/paste, breaking PEM parsing |
| Frontend auth race condition (client) | Added a `loading` state to `AuthContext`, gated redirects on it | `ProtectedRoute` was checking login state before Firebase's `onAuthStateChanged` listener resolved, causing a false bounce to `/login` |
| Prisma/OpenSSL Docker mismatch (provider) | Pinned `binaryTargets` and added `openssl` to the Docker build stage | Prisma's query engine was generated for a different OpenSSL version than the Alpine runtime container had |
| JWT audience validation | Accept both bare client ID and `api://<client-id>` URI form, as an array | Azure issues either format depending on how the token was requested; a single hardcoded value failed every request |
| JWT issuer validation | Set `requestedAccessTokenVersion: 2` in the app registration's **new** Microsoft Graph manifest | Azure was issuing v1-format tokens by default despite MSAL using the v2 authority; the setting lives in a different place in the old (deprecating) manifest editor |
