heading: The Full End-to-End Sync Test (2026-08-01)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## The Full End-to-End Sync Test (2026-08-01)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## The Full End-to-End Sync Test (2026-08-01)

This is where the real integration bugs surfaced — each side worked independently, but connecting them for the first time exposed **7 distinct issues**, all found and fixed in one session:

| # | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Provider frontend sent `snake_case` fields (`premium_amount`) to an API expecting `camelCase` (`premiumAmount`) on the catalog form | Fixed frontend to match the API |
| 2 | Docker networking: client API calling `http://localhost:4100` to reach the provider API failed with a bare "fetch failed" | Switched to `http://host.docker.internal:4100` — `localhost` inside a container refers to the container itself, not sibling containers |
| 3 | Client's catalog-sync read `item.premium_amount` from a response that's actually `item.premiumAmount` | Fixed to read correct camelCase fields |
| 4 | Enrollment sync payload was missing `client_user_ref` entirely, which the provider requires | Added the enrolling user's Firebase UID as the reference |
| 5 | Enrollment payload sent the client's own local catalog cache ID instead of the provider's actual catalog ID | Fixed to send the correct cross-referenced `providerPolicyId` |
| 6 | A new enrollment's `providerPolicyId` was set prematurely, causing the sync logic to misidentify every first enrollment as a "renewal" | Left the field null until the provider's response confirms its own new record's ID |
| 7 | Same Docker networking issue as #2, but in reverse (provider calling back to client) — **plus** a second bug once networking was fixed: the client's inbound status-sync routes read fields directly off `req.body` instead of unwrapping the standard envelope | Fixed networking the same way as #2; added the same `unwrap()` pattern the provider's own code already used correctly |

**What happened next:** once all 7 bugs were fixed on the enrollment/activation path, the **remaining three sync paths** — premium payment, claim submission, and all 3 claim status transitions (Under Review → Approved → Paid) — were tested live and passed with **zero additional bugs**. The foundational fixes (Docker networking, envelope unwrapping, camelCase field handling) carried through cleanly to every other endpoint.

**Result:** the full happy-path journey — enroll → provider activates → pay premium → file claim → review → approve → mark paid → dashboard shows complete history — now runs correctly end-to-end, live, across both clouds, with real data, exactly as designed back in Phase 2.

---

heading: Production Deployment (Phase 4)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Production Deployment (Phase 4)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Production Deployment (Phase 4)

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| No custom domain | Used free `nip.io` wildcard DNS instead of buying a domain | Keeps the project at $0 for domain costs; `nip.io` resolves any IP into a usable hostname, which is all Let's Encrypt needs to issue a real certificate |
| Frontend hosting | Both frontends deployed to Vercel, not VM-hosted | Matches the original Phase 1 plan; static frontends don't need a server, so a managed CDN platform is simpler and free, versus self-hosting on a VM for no real benefit |
| GCP client API deployment | Static IP reserved, firewall opened only on 80/443 (never the raw app port 4000), `e2-micro` VM in `us-central1`, Docker + Nginx + Let's Encrypt | Matches the free-tier-eligible plan from Phase 4 planning; keeping port 4000 closed and routing everything through Nginx on 80/443 is the correct security posture, not just a workaround |
| Azure provider API deployment | Ended up on `Standard_D2ads_v6` in `centralus` (~$22.66/month) instead of the originally planned free-tier `B1s`/`B2s` in `eastus` | Multiple region/size combinations hit capacity restrictions; the subscription also needed upgrading from Free Trial to Pay-As-You-Go before VM quota was usable at all. The working combination was found through direct trial across regions/sizes rather than guesswork |
| Branch protection self-approval block | Set "Required approvals" to 0 on all 4 repos before merging any `dev`→`main` PR | GitHub blocks a solo account from approving its own PR, even as repo owner/admin — discovered when the first PR got stuck indefinitely on "Awaiting approval" |
| `dev` → `main` merge discipline | All 4 repos merged before any deployment, establishing `main` as "what's actually running in production" | Keeps a clean release boundary — deployments pull from `main`, active work stays on `dev` |
| Docker Compose env var gaps | Two separate cases where a variable existed correctly in `.env` and the app code, but was missing from `docker-compose.yml`'s explicit environment list — so the running container silently never received it | The compose files list env vars explicitly rather than loading the whole `.env` file; a var added to the app after the compose file was written can be missed. Fixed by adding the missing lines and forcing a full `docker compose down` + `up` (not just `--build`, which doesn't always pick up compose-file changes) |
| SPA routing on Vercel | Added a `vercel.json` rewrite rule so any non-asset path serves `index.html` | React Router SPAs only have `index.html` as a real static file on Vercel; direct navigation or a refresh on any other route (like `/login`) 404s without this rule — a standard, well-known requirement for this hosting pattern |
| Hardcoded MSAL redirect URI | Changed `redirectUri`/`postLogoutRedirectUri` from a hardcoded `localhost:5174` string to `window.location.origin` | The original code only worked locally; deployed to Vercel, it kept trying to redirect back to `localhost`, causing a connection-refused error. `window.location.origin` resolves correctly in any environment automatically |
| Cross-cloud production URLs | Updated both APIs' `.env` files to point at each other's real deployed HTTPS URLs, replacing the local `host.docker.internal` addressing used during Phase 3 testing | Local Docker networking tricks don't apply once each side is on its own real VM; production sync needs real public URLs |

**Result so far:** both APIs are live with valid SSL certificates, both frontends are live on Vercel, and the provider side has been independently verified end-to-end in production (Entra ID login, role detection, catalog creation). Full cross-cloud sync re-verification against the live production deployment is still pending.

---

heading: Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (Phase 5)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (Phase 5)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Documentation & Multi-Agent Orchestration (Phase 5)

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile responsive nav (provider) | Added a hamburger menu collapsing below 768px, desktop layout untouched | The multi-link nav overlapped page content on small screens; a full menu made sense given how many links/items it holds |
| Mobile responsive nav (client) | Used a lighter CSS-only stacking fix instead of a hamburger | This nav only has 2 links + username + Logout — a hamburger would have been overkill for that little content; matched the fix's complexity to the actual UI |
| Documentation trio, all 4 repos | Added `BUSINESS_REQUIREMENTS.md`, updated `README.md`, added `CLAUDE.md` to every repo | Gives future sessions (human or AI) the "what and why" plus every hard-won gotcha, instead of re-discovering the same bugs; the `CLAUDE.md` files doubled as the knowledge base for the subagents built next |
| Master/subagent orchestration | Built on Claude Code's native subagent feature — a parent session (`agent-vkai-master`) at the folder above all 4 repos, plus 4 scoped subagents in `.claude/agents/` | Lets a plain-English requirement get routed automatically to the right repo(s), with the human still approving the plan before anything is touched — genuine delegation, not just "one big agent doing everything" |
| Subagent scope isolation | Convention-based (explicit instructions), not a technical sandbox | Matches the same trust model already used everywhere else in this project — subagents are told to only touch their own repo and flag anything else, rather than being hard-walled off |
| Story tracking | A single append-only `Story.md` at the parent folder, `VKAI-XXX` numbered | Simple audit trail without needing an external tool like Jira for a personal project |
| Story numbering rule | Honor a human-given `VKAI-XXX` number if provided, otherwise auto-assign the next one | Keeps numbering flexible — the human can pre-plan story numbers, or just let the system handle it |
| Subagents never merge PRs | They commit + push to their own `dev` branch only | Matches the human-in-the-loop discipline used for every other change across this whole project — no code reaches `main` without a human reviewing it |
| Doc-update rule added to all subagents | Retrofitted after VKAI-001 shipped without updating either repo's docs | The first real story exposed the gap live; fixed by adding a standing rule so every future story keeps its own repo's docs current as part of the same commit, not a separate afterthought |
| Git identity fix | Set global `user.name`/`user.email`, discovered they'd never been configured | Every commit across the whole project had silently been authored under a placeholder machine identity; fixed going forward (not retroactively, not worth rewriting already-merged history for cosmetic authorship) |

**First real test — VKAI-001:** a genuinely non-trivial story (an auto-generated, locked "key" field on policy catalog entries, with collision handling) was routed through the system for real. The master correctly identified it as provider-side-only, **asked clarifying questions before proposing anything**, sequenced the two affected subagents correctly (API before frontend), and one subagent made an unprompted, correct security judgment call (excluding the new field from the cross-cloud endpoint so it never leaks to the client side) — flagging the decision clearly rather than making it silently. Verified live in production, including a fresh full E2E cross-cloud test to confirm nothing regressed.

---

heading: CI/CD Pipelines (Phase 6)
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## CI/CD Pipelines (Phase 6)
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## CI/CD Pipelines (Phase 6)

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy trigger | GitHub Actions on `push: main`, API repos only | Frontends already auto-deploy via Vercel; only the two API repos needed new pipeline work |
| Deploy keys | Dedicated SSH keypair per VM, not the owner's personal key | Keeps each cloud's automated access fully independent |
| `~` path bug | Switched to absolute paths in remote SSH scripts | `~` doesn't reliably expand in `appleboy/ssh-action`'s non-interactive shell |
| Secret mix-up | Found via temporary debug output (`whoami`, `hostname`), not more guessing | Client-api repo's `DEPLOY_HOST` secret had been set to the *provider's* IP by mistake |
| Health-check timing | `sleep 20` + 5-attempt retry loop, not a single early `curl` | Postgres healthcheck + Prisma migration + API boot takes longer than a flat 5-second wait |
| `dev`→`main` merge | Deliberately left as the one manual step, not automated | Keeps a human checkpoint before anything goes live in production |

**Result:** both API repos now auto-deploy to production on every merge to `main`, confirmed working via multiple real pipeline runs.

heading: VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation
breadcrumb: # VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation
text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## VKAI-002 — Cross-Cloud Key Propagation

| Scope reversal | Re-opened and reversed VKAI-001's decision to exclude `key` from the cross-cloud endpoint | Real requirements evolved — a good example of documenting *why* a reversal happens rather than silently changing it |

| Docker image gap | Added missing `COPY scripts ./scripts` to the Dockerfile | Same category of bug as the earlier `docker-compose.yml` env var gaps — a new folder wasn't in the image's explicit copy list |

text:
# VK AI Labs Insurance Ecosystem — What We Did & Why > ## Public Showcase Website (Phase 9)

| Keyword | What we did | Why we did it |
|---|---|---|
| Separate repo | `vkai-labs-showcase`, sibling to `insurance/`, own dedicated agent | Outside `agent-vkai-master`'s scope — a portfolio site, not a 5th orchestrated repo |
| Plain HTML/CSS/JS | No framework, no build step | Deploys to Vercel as a static site with zero build config |
| Diagram sourcing | Used fresh `.drawio`-native PNGs instead of the existing HTML/SVG exports | Headless rendering of the HTML sources surfaced real, unresolved layout bugs (clipped columns, a dropped text step, overlapping labels) — not just screenshot artifacts |
| Pointer-events trap | Root-caused to `.lightbox{display:flex}` beating `[hidden]{display:none}` on CSS specificity | Explains why keyboard nav worked but mouse clicks didn't across the whole site |
| `:focus-visible` bug | Replaced with a manual `user-is-tabbing` body-class pattern | Browser heuristics for programmatic `.focus()` calls are inconsistent — Chrome showed the ring even on mouse clicks |
| Git identity check | Baked into the new agent as a mandatory pre-push step | A wrong-account (`sharmalily1984-cloud` vs `vkailabs`) mix-up was caught mid-build |

**Result:** a four-slide portfolio showcase (Intro → Architecture → AI Orchestration → System Flow + live portal links), built via Claude Code, debugged to real root causes rather than patched at the symptom level, deployed live under the `vkailabs` org, with its own dedicated `agent_VKAI_showcase` maintenance agent for future changes.
